哪里有为了让饥饿的人们有饭吃而进行的斗争，我都会在那里。哪里有警察殴打民众，我都会在那里。我会在人们愤怒呐喊的场景中，也会在孩子们饥饿时欢笑，因为他们知道晚饭已经准备好了的场景中。当我们的同胞吃着自己种植的粮食，住在自己建造的房屋里时——我也会在那里。

But these ideas don’t really get to the heart of epistrophe. They use it, but they don’t inhabit it. Because epistrophe, usually, by its very form, has an underlying sense of No you can’t . Whatever you try to do, however you start out, you’ll always end up at the same place, back where you started, as with the songs above. It just so happens that Mr Obama’s starting point was Yes we can . But epistrophe is much more natural when you’re in trouble. When Henry V has traitors brought before him, he says:

但这些想法并没有真正触及尾韵的精髓。他们运用了尾韵，却没有真正理解它的含义。因为尾韵通常从其形式本身就蕴含着一种“不，你做不到”的意味。无论你尝试做什么，无论你如何开始，最终都会回到原点，就像上面提到的歌曲一样。奥巴马先生的出发点恰好是“是的，我们能”。但尾韵在困境中显得更加自然。当亨利五世将叛徒带到他面前时，他说：

Show men dutiful?

展现男人的尽职尽责？

Why, so didst thou: seem they grave and learned?

你为何如此认为：他们看起来严肃而有学问？

Why, so didst thou: come they of noble family?

为什么你也这样：他们出身名门？

Why, so didst thou: seem they religious?

你为何如此认为：他们看起来虔诚吗？

Why, so didst thou.

你也一样。

And you know he’s angry. You know that they aren’t getting out of this one. And indeed they don’t get out of this one. Henry executes the lot of them. Wherever you start out, you’re going to finish up with so didst thou . And whatever they say, their necks are marked for the chopping block.

你知道他很生气。你知道他们这次逃不掉了。而事实也的确如此。亨利把他们全都处决了。无论你从哪里开始，最终都会落得同样的下场。不管他们说什么，他们的脖子都已经被标记，等着被砍下来。

In fact, epistrophe is particularly suited for death; I suppose because death is the huge human epistrophe, and all biographies end the same way. Thus the technique seems so suitable in Psalm 118 where we run through a list of nations and people and find, in each case, that ‘in the name of the Lord, I will destroy them’. Epistrophe is probably at its most natural in the film Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels , 2 where an angry gang boss explains his terms to a rather unfortunate fellow who’s accidentally crossed him.

事实上，尾韵尤其适合用来描述死亡；我想是因为死亡是人类漫长的尾韵，而所有人生的最终结局都相同。因此，这种修辞手法在诗篇118篇中显得尤为贴切，我们逐一浏览各国各族，发现每一种情况都以“奉耶和华的名，我必毁灭他们”结尾。尾韵最自然的运用或许是在电影《两杆大烟枪》中，片中一位愤怒的黑帮老大向一位不小心得罪了他的倒霉蛋解释他的条件。

If you hold back anything, I’ll kill you. If you bend the truth, or I think you’re bending the truth, I’ll kill you. If you forget anything, I’ll kill you. In fact, you’re going to have to work very hard to stay alive, Nick. Now, do you understand everything I’ve said? Because if you don’t, I’ll kill you.

如果你有所隐瞒，我就杀了你。如果你歪曲事实，或者我认为你在歪曲事实，我就杀了你。如果你忘记了什么，我就杀了你。事实上，尼克，你得非常努力才能活下去。现在，你都明白我说的了吗？如果你不明白，我就杀了你。

Death is an epistrophe and epistrophe is death. But …

死亡是尾韵，尾韵即是死亡。但是……

Epistrophe works wonderfully with a good but . You demonstrate that all the doors are closed. This door is closed. That door is closed. The other door is closed. And then you point out the fire exit.

尾音转折与一个好的“但是”搭配使用效果极佳。你可以先说明所有的门都关上了。这扇门关上了。那扇门关上了。还有一扇门也关上了。然后你指出消防出口。

It’s used a little clumsily by Aragorn in the film of The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King when he tells everyone that:

在电影《指环王：王者归来》中，阿拉贡略显笨拙地使用了这个词，他告诉大家：

A day may come when the courage of men fails, when we forsake our friends and break all bonds of fellowship, but it is not this day. An hour of woes and shattered shields, when the age of men comes crashing down! But it is not this day! This day we fight!

或许有一天，男儿的勇气会消逝，我们会抛弃朋友，断绝一切情谊，但那一天并非今日。或许有一天，苦难会降临，盾牌会破碎，人类的时代会轰然崩塌！但那一天并非今日！今日，我们战斗！

Slightly better is Saint Paul who finds himself in an epistrophe and then, inevitably, finds his way out:

稍微好一点的是圣保罗，他发现自己陷入了尾声，然后，不可避免地，找到了出路：

When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things. For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known. And now abideth faith, hope, love, these three; but the greatest of these is love.

我作孩子的时候，话语像孩子，心思像孩子，意念像孩子；既成了人，就把孩子的事丢弃了。我们如今仿佛对着镜子观看，模糊不清；到那时就要面对面了。我如今所知道的有限；到那时就全知道，如同主知道我一样。如今常存的有信，有望，有爱，这三样，其中最大的是爱。

Faith, hope and love is a good example of a tricolon.

信仰、希望和爱是三段式的一个很好的例子。

1 It is a principle and rhetorical trick you should never teach to small children.

1 这是你绝对不应该教给小孩子的原则和修辞技巧。

2 By Mr Guy Ritchie, released in 1998.

2 由盖·里奇执导，于 1998 年上映。

# ↩

Chapter 16

第十六章

Tricolon

三列

I came; I saw; I conquered.

我来过；我见过；我征服过。

Sun, sea and sex.

阳光、大海和性。

Three is the magic number of literary composition, but to explain why that is you have to look at the much more boring number two.

三是文学创作的神奇数字，但要解释为什么会这样，你必须看看更乏味的数字二。

Whenever the average human sees two things together, they connect them. So if I say the words eat and drink , you will, unless you’re a bit weird, notice that those are the two major forms of ingestion. 1 You might also see eat and drink as opposites: solid vs. liquid. The same thought will occur to you if I mention the father and the son or the good and the bad or truth and justice.

普通人看到两样东西放在一起时，都会把它们联系起来。所以，如果我说“吃”和“喝”，除非你有点怪癖，否则你会注意到这是两种主要的摄入方式。¹ 你可能还会把“吃”和“喝”看作是对立的：固体与液体。如果我提到父亲和儿子、善与恶、真理和正义，你也会想到同样的事情。

Even if we take two things that don’t fit together we’ll find something. Mice and men? Well, they’re … they’re small and big? Cabbages and kings? One is familiar and domestic and the other grand and distant? That’s just how the human brain is built, and it’s all the fault of God and Darwin. We see a pair and we see a pattern.

即使我们把两个看似毫不相干的事物放在一起，也能从中发现某种联系。老鼠和人？嗯，它们……一个渺小，一个庞大？卷心菜和国王？一个熟悉亲切，另一个高大威严？这正是人类大脑的构造，而这一切都要归功于上帝和达尔文。我们看到一对事物，就能发现其中的规律。

You can always, always connect two dots with a straight line.

你总能用直线连接两点。

But add another word and they’re tricolons. Eat, drink and be merry. Father, Son and Holy Spirit. The Good, the Bad and the Ugly. Truth, justice and the American way.

但再加一个词，它们就成了三连句。吃喝玩乐。圣父、圣子和圣灵。善、恶、丑。真理、正义和美国精神。

With a tricolon you can set up a pattern and then break it. ‘Lies, damned lies, and statistics’ is a simple example. The first two words establish the direction we’re going. The third twists things for humorous purposes. This is, incidentally, the structure of a particular kind of joke. Did you hear the one about three people in a peculiar situation? The first two do something sensible, but the third does something really odd! It doesn’t matter whether you populate it with priests and rabbis, or with Englishmen, Irishmen and Scotsmen; it’s always the same basic joke.

三段式结构可以先建立一种模式，然后再打破它。“谎言、该死的谎言和统计数据”就是一个简单的例子。前两个词确定了我们前进的方向，第三个词则为了达到幽默的效果而扭转了局面。顺便一提，这也是一种特定笑话的结构。你听过那个关于三个身处奇特境地的人的笑话吗？前两个人做了合情合理的事，但第三个人却做了件非常古怪的事！无论你把故事里的人物换成牧师和拉比，还是英国人、爱尔兰人和苏格兰人，都无关紧要；笑话的基本套路始终不变。

The surprise can be based purely on sound. Alliteration provides the twist of ‘Wine, women and song’ and rhyme gives it to ‘Ready, steady, go’.

这种惊喜可以完全源于声音。头韵赋予了“美酒、佳人和歌声”以韵律感，而押韵则让“预备，稳住，出发”更具冲击力。

Or the surprise can simply be for the sake of surprise. ‘It’s a bird! It’s a plane! It’s Superman!’ The famous Superman opening is a whirl of tricolons, and tricolons planted within tricolons. It begins with a surprise one, and it ends with an extender: truth, justice and the American way. 2

或者，惊喜本身就是一种惊喜。“是鸟！是飞机！是超人！”著名的超人开场白是一连串的三段式，而且三段式层层嵌套。它以一个令人意想不到的开头，以一个延伸句结尾：真理、正义和美国精神。

Tricolons sound great if the third thing is longer. The American way is (as outlined in their mutinous Declaration of Independence) made up of life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. The pursuit of happiness is, if you think about it, the least of the promises here. You can pursue happiness as much as you like, and most of us do anyway. It rarely ends in capture. Life and liberty were the more important guarantees. But it sounds so good when you go on a bit at the end. ‘Friends, Romans, countrymen’ works the same way. In terms of content Antony would have been much better off starting with the fact that they’re all of the same nationality, then pointing out that they are Romans, and finally, in a gushy sort of way, pointing out that they are really friends too. But the longest bit of the tricolon must be saved for last, even if it’s the least important. Lady Caroline Lamb knew this when she called Byron ‘Mad, bad and dangerous to know’. And Shakespeare knew it when he wrote: ‘We few, we happy few, we band of brothers’, or ‘of graves, of worms and epitaphs’, or … when it comes to tricolons, Shakespeare had been there, done that, and bought the T-shirt.

如果第三项内容更长，三段式句听起来会更精彩。美国人的生活方式（正如他们在叛逆的《独立宣言》中所阐述的）由生命、自由和追求幸福构成。仔细想想，追求幸福其实是这三项承诺中最不重要的。你可以尽情追求幸福，而且我们大多数人也确实如此。追求幸福很少会导致被捕。生命和自由才是更重要的保障。但如果在结尾多写一些，听起来就更棒了。“朋友们，罗马人，同胞们”也是如此。就内容而言，安东尼最好先指出他们拥有相同的国籍，然后指出他们是罗马人，最后用一种略带热情的方式指出他们也是真正的朋友。但三段式句中最长的部分必须留到最后，即使它最不重要。卡罗琳·兰姆夫人深谙此道，她称拜伦为“疯子、坏人，而且认识他很危险”。莎士比亚也深知这一点，他写道：“我们少数人，我们幸福的少数人，我们兄弟连”，或者“坟墓，蠕虫和墓志铭”，或者……说到三段式，莎士比亚早已驾轻就熟，深谙此道。

In fact, there’s something nasty, brutish and short 3 about some tricolons, which just punch you with three words. The French should have seen where the revolution would end up when it got the motto Liberté, Egalité, Fraternité . That’s dictatorship right there. The Germans got shorter still with Ein Reich! Ein Volk! Ein Führer! and sent all their Fräuleins off to look after the Kinder, Küche, Kirche .

事实上，有些三连句（或称三冒号）简洁粗暴，仿佛三个词就狠狠地打了你一巴掌。法国人当初就应该预料到，当革命的口号是“自由、平等、博爱”时，最终会走向何方。这不就是独裁吗？德国人更进一步，用了“帝国！民族！元首！”这三个词，然后把所有的小姐都打发去照顾“儿童、厨房、教堂”。

Sometimes the tricolon goes in exactly the direction you expected, but this is actually rather rare. There’s Rick in Casablanca complaining about ‘all the gin-joints, in all the towns, in all the world’, and there’s Douglas Adams’ great question of ‘life, the universe, and everything’. But lengthening and surprise are much more important and much more powerful.

有时，三连句的走向会完全符合你的预期，但这其实相当罕见。比如《卡萨布兰卡》里的里克抱怨“全世界所有城镇的所有酒吧”，还有道格拉斯·亚当斯提出的“生命、宇宙以及一切”的伟大问题。但句式的延长和出人意料的出现更为重要，也更有力量。

Another problem with the rising tricolon is that it has to get to the end. When you go up, you can’t stop halfway. That’s why Rick has to get to the realistic upper limit of the world, and the galactic hitchhiker to the preposterous upper limit of everything. Two’s company, three’s a list, and a list has to be complete.

上升三段式句式的另一个问题是，它必须到达终点。上升时，你不能中途停下来。这就是为什么里克必须到达世界的现实上限，而银河系搭便车者必须到达一切事物的荒谬上限。两人成伴，三人成列，而清单必须完整。

That’s the final and most important aspect of the tricolon. The good and the bad together make up two sides of the moral coin. The Good, the Bad and the Ugly is a list of the major characters in a film. Eat and drink are two methods of ingestion. Eat, drink and be merry is a list of all the things you need to do this evening. Father and son is a generational pair: Father, Son and Holy Ghost is a list of all the aspects of God. When you finish a tricolon, you finish because there is nothing more to say. You’ve said it all. The list is complete. These are the final words.

这是三句句的最后一个也是最重要的方面。“好”与“坏”共同构成了道德硬币的两面。“好人、坏人和丑人”是电影中主要角色的列表。“吃”和“喝”是两种摄入方式。“吃喝玩乐”列出了你今晚需要做的所有事情。“父与子”是世代关系：“父、子与圣灵”列出了上帝的所有方面。当你完成一个三句句时，就意味着已经无话可说。你已经把所有想说的都说完了。列表已经完整。这就是最后的话语。

This sense of completeness makes the tricolon perfectly suited to grand rhetoric. That’s why Barack Obama packed 21 tricolons into his short victory speech. Tricolons sound statesmanlike. It’s government of the people, by the people, for the people. Even though I can’t for the life of me see what the difference is between ‘of the people’ and ‘by the people’, it doesn’t matter. It’s three and three sounds good.

这种完整性使得三段式格律非常适合宏大的修辞。这就是为什么巴拉克·奥巴马在他简短的胜选演讲中用了21个三段式格律。三段式格律听起来很有政治家风范。它代表着民有、民治、民享的政府。尽管我百思不得其解“民有”和“民治”之间的区别，但这并不重要。重要的是三个字母，而三个字母听起来很和谐。

Two is only a pair, and four is all wrong. Churchill tried a four (it’s called a tetracolon). In his first speech to Parliament as Prime Minister he told them that he had ‘nothing to offer but blood, toil, tears and sweat’. But four doesn’t work and everybody remembers the line as ‘blood, sweat and tears’. 4

二只能算一对，四则完全错误。丘吉尔尝试过四（这叫做四重冒号）。在他作为首相首次向议会发表的演讲中，他告诉议员们，他“除了鲜血、辛劳、眼泪和汗水之外，别无他物”。但四行不通，所以大家都记住了“鲜血、汗水和眼泪”这句话。<sup>4</sup>

It is always three and never four. Estate agents do not rely on the rule location, location, location, location, although that would still be an example of epizeuxis.

永远是三，绝不会是四。房地产经纪人并不依赖“地段、地段、地段、地段”这条规则，尽管这仍然属于过度依赖的范畴。

1 There was a brief nineteenth - century fad for putting food up your bottom. President James Garfield was fed this way for a month. Then he died. For information you may consult Feeding Per Rectum by Doctor William Bliss (1882). The colon and the tricolon do not, unfortunately, have even an etymological connection.

19世纪曾短暂流行过一种从肛门进食的风潮。詹姆斯·加菲尔德总统就曾这样进食一个月，之后便去世了。欲了解更多信息，可参阅威廉·布利斯医生于1882年撰写的《直肠进食》（Feeding Per Rectum）。遗憾的是，结肠和三结肠在词源上并无关联。

2 I suppose this might be classed as a surprise tricolon by politically active, sincere, tedious people.

2 我想，对于政治活跃、真诚、乏味的人来说，这或许可以算作一个令人惊讶的三连句。

3 Hobbes’ original line was ‘the life of man, solitary, poor, nasty, brutish and short’ but memory has corrected the number.

3 霍布斯的原话是“人的生命，孤独、贫穷、肮脏、野蛮而短暂”，但记忆已经纠正了这个数字。

4 The origins of this phrase are rather complicated. Churchill never said ‘blood, sweat and tears’ but Thomas Jefferson did in 1897, and Lord Alfred Douglas said ‘Blood and sweat and tears’ in 1919. However, my point here is that everybody remembers it as a Churchill line, or, more precisely, misremembers that Churchill line by making it a tricolon. Also, Churchill never said ‘Rum, sodomy and the lash’.

4 这句话的起源相当复杂。丘吉尔从未说过“血汗泪”，但托马斯·杰斐逊在1897年说过，阿尔弗雷德·道格拉斯勋爵在1919年也说过。然而，我想说的是，大家都把它当作丘吉尔的名言，或者更准确地说，是误记了丘吉尔的名言，把它变成了三连句。另外，丘吉尔也从未说过“朗姆酒、鸡奸和鞭笞”。

# ↩

Chapter 17

第十七章

Epizeuxis

埃皮泽克西斯

This book is about one tiny, tiny aspect of rhetoric: the figures of speech. There are all sorts of other bits to the subject: arguing, proving, inventing, memorising, and delivery. When an Ancient Greek chap was learning rhetoric he even had to learn the correct hand gestures, or actions , to be used at different points in the speech. The great orator Demosthenes was once asked what the three most important things in rhetoric were, and he replied: ‘Action. Action. Action.’

这本书只探讨了修辞学中一个极其微小的方面：修辞格。修辞学还包含许多其他方面：论证、证明、创造、记忆和表达。古希腊人学习修辞学时，甚至还要学习在演讲的不同阶段应该使用的正确手势或动作。伟大的演说家德摩斯梯尼曾被问及修辞学中最重要的三件事是什么，他回答说：“行动。行动。行动。”

History does not record how he gestured as he said this. He may have punched the air or twiddled his thumbs. All we know is what he said, and how he said it: with epizeuxis.

历史并未记载他说话时的手势。他或许挥舞着拳头，或许摆弄着拇指。我们只知道他说了什么，以及他说话的方式：带着一种略带夸张的语气。

Epizeuxis (pronounced ep-ee-ZOOX-is) is repeating a word immediately in exactly the same sense. Simple. Simple. Simple. However, epizeuxis is not the easiest way to get into the dictionary of quotations. It’s like a nuclear bomb: immensely effective, but a bit weird if you use it every five minutes.

Epizeuxis（发音为ep-ee-ZOOX-is）指的是立即重复一个词，且含义完全相同。就这么简单。然而，Epizeuxis并非进入引语词典的最佳途径。它就像一颗核弹：威力巨大，但如果每五分钟就用一次，那就有点怪异了。

Demosthenes was using epizeuxis for the very old joke of enumerating the same thing. Twenty-three centuries later it was still being used in lines like: ‘The first rule of Fight Club is: you do not talk about Fight Club. The second rule of Fight Club is: you do not talk about Fight Club.’ 1 But the pure epizeuxis form is still around as well. Since the 1920s it has been a maxim of American real estate agents that the three most important things about a property are ‘location, location, location’. In 1996 Tony Blair told the Labour Party conference: ‘Ask me my three main priorities for government and I tell you: education, education and education.’ Mr Blair had, almost certainly, stolen the joke from real estate agents, but it goes back to Demosthenes.

德摩斯梯尼使用“重复句”（epizeuxis）来表达一个非常古老的笑话，即列举同一件事。23个世纪后，它仍然出现在诸如“搏击俱乐部第一条规则是：不要谈论搏击俱乐部。搏击俱乐部第二条规则是：不要谈论搏击俱乐部。”¹ 但纯粹的重复句形式也依然存在。自20世纪20年代以来，美国房地产经纪人一直奉行一条格言：房产最重要的三件事是“地段、地段、地段”。1996年，托尼·布莱尔在工党大会上说：“问我政府的三大优先事项是什么，我会告诉你：教育、教育、还是教育。” 布莱尔先生几乎可以肯定是从房地产经纪人那里“借鉴”了这个笑话，但它的起源可以追溯到德摩斯梯尼。

‘Education, education, education’ got the biggest round of applause and the best headlines of the party conference, which is probably why Blair decided to try epizeuxis again three months later during Prime Minister’s questions. He wasn’t Prime Minister at the time, instead poor John Major was in charge and trying to control the wild and bloodthirsty menagerie commonly known as the Conservative Party. Tony Blair said: ‘Isn’t it extraordinary that the Prime Minister of our country can’t even urge his Party to back his own position? Weak! Weak! Weak!’ And again he hit the headlines, but this time the three words were being used not as the Demosthenian joke: this was epizeuxis for intensification.

“教育，教育，教育”这句口号赢得了党代会最热烈的掌声和最热门的头条新闻，这或许也是为什么三个月后，布莱尔在首相质询环节再次使用“强化”（epizeuxis）一词的原因。当时他并非首相，而是由可怜的约翰·梅杰掌权，他正努力控制着那群被称为保守党的狂野而嗜血的乌合之众。托尼·布莱尔说道：“我们国家的首相竟然连自己的党都无法敦促其支持自己的立场，这难道不令人匪夷所思吗？软弱！软弱！软弱！”他又一次登上了头条，但这一次，这三个字并非是德摩斯梯尼式的玩笑：而是用来强化语气的“强化”（epizeuxis）。

Back in 1994 Tony Blair told an interviewer that ‘The art of leadership is saying no’, a point that he had probably learnt from Margaret Thatcher. She outlined her position on Europe to the House of Commons with three words: ‘No. No. No.’ It so happens that in the context of the debate she was answering three rather precise points made by Jacques Delors, the President of the European Commission. The full line reads like this:

早在1994年，托尼·布莱尔就曾对一位采访者说，“领导的艺术在于说‘不’”，这一点他很可能是从玛格丽特·撒切尔那里学来的。撒切尔在下议院用三个字阐述了她对欧洲问题的立场：“不，不，不。” 巧合的是，在那场辩论中，她正是回应了欧盟委员会主席雅克·德洛尔提出的三个非常具体的观点。完整内容如下：

‘The President of the Commission, M. Delors, said at a press conference the other day that he wanted the European Parliament to be the democratic body of the Community, he wanted the Commission to be the Executive and he wanted the Council of Ministers to be the Senate. No. No. No.’

“欧盟委员会主席德洛尔先生前几天在新闻发布会上说，他希望欧洲议会成为共同体的民主机构，欧盟委员会成为执行机构，部长理事会成为参议院。不，不，不。”

But all that’s remembered is the emphatic epizeuxis of ‘No. No. No.’, where the repetition is no numerical joke, but a sign of emotion, conviction and emphasis, just as in Macbeth you have, ‘O horror, horror, horror’, and in King Lear , ‘Howl! Howl! Howl! Howl!’ King Lear is here breaking the golden rule of three, which is a sign, I suppose, of his madness. His last speech is an exercise in epizeuxis:

但人们记住的只有那句强调的“不，不，不”，这里的重复并非数字上的玩笑，而是情感、信念和强调的象征，正如《麦克白》中的“哦，恐怖，恐怖，恐怖”，以及《李尔王》中的“嚎叫！嚎叫！嚎叫！嚎叫！”。李尔王在这里打破了三的黄金法则，我想，这或许是他疯狂的标志。他最后的独白是对重复手法的一次精妙运用：

And my poor fool is hang’d! No, no, no life!

我可怜的傻瓜被绞死了！不，不，没命了！

Why should a dog, a horse, a rat, have life,

为什么狗、马、老鼠就应该拥有生命？

And thou no breath at all? Thou’lt come no more,

你竟没有一丝气息？你再也不会来了。

Never, never, never, never, never!

绝不，绝不，绝不，绝不，绝不！

Pray you, undo this button: thank you, sir.

请您撤销这个按钮：谢谢您，先生。

Do you see this? Look on her, look, her lips,

你看到了吗？看看她，看看她的嘴唇。

Look there, look there!

看那里，看那里！

[ Dies ]

[去世]

There is a popular story that Henry VIII died on an epizeuxis. He is meant to have gazed into the dark corners of the room and shrieked ‘Monks! Monks! Monks!’ It’s complete nonsense and seems to have been dreamt up in the mid-nineteenth century, but the story has survived because it sounds right. In fact, Henry VIII was speechless on his deathbed and only managed, apparently, to squeeze the Archbishop of Canterbury’s hand when asked if he trusted in God. Perhaps, though, the monks would have been even more dramatic had they been mumbled.

坊间流传着一个说法，亨利八世死于一场惊恐发作。据说他当时凝视着房间的黑暗角落，高声喊着“僧侣！僧侣！僧侣！”。这完全是无稽之谈，似乎是十九世纪中期编造出来的，但这个故事流传至今，因为它听起来合情合理。事实上，亨利八世在临终前一句话也说不出来，据说他唯一能做的，就是在被问及是否信仰上帝时，握了握坎特伯雷大主教的手。不过，如果僧侣们只是喃喃自语，或许会显得更加戏剧化。

Epizeuxis is ambiguous. Sometimes it means a moment of intense emotion, and sometimes an inescapable drone. The actor playing King Lear can either scream the words ‘Never, never, never, never, never!’ or mumble them. He can’t do much in between. Repetition can mean … repetition, repetition, repetition on and on and on and on for ever and ever. ‘Tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow / Creeps into this petty place’ is clearly a case of a man resigning himself to the dull, inevitable future. The same resignation of Alfred Lord Tennyson watching the waves and saying: ‘Break, break, break, / On thy cold grey stones, O Sea!’

“Epizeuxis”一词含义模糊。有时它指强烈的情感爆发，有时又指挥之不去的单调重复。扮演李尔王的演员可以嘶吼着“永不，永不，永不，永不，永不！”，也可以低声喃喃。他几乎无法做到介于两者之间的任何状态。重复可以意味着……无休止的重复，永无止境。“明天，明天，明天/悄悄潜入这渺小之地”显然是一个人无奈地接受沉闷而不可避免的未来。这与阿尔弗雷德·丁尼生勋爵望着海浪吟唱的“破碎吧，破碎吧，破碎吧，/在你冰冷的灰色石头上，哦，大海！”所表达的无奈如出一辙。

This quieter form of epizeuxis can even be dismissive. When Polonius asks Hamlet what he’s reading, Hamlet replies, ‘Words, words, words’ in a way that implies perhaps only a shrug. And maybe that the book is too long. It’s the same bored condescension that was implied by Prince William, Duke of Gloucester when he was presented with the second volume of Gibbon’s Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire : ‘Another damned thick book! Always scribble, scribble, scribble! Eh, Mr Gibbon?’

这种较为平静的沉思甚至带有轻蔑的意味。当波洛涅斯问哈姆雷特在读什么书时，哈姆雷特回答说：“文字，文字，文字”，语气中或许只是耸了耸肩，或许还暗示着这本书太长了。这与格洛斯特公爵威廉王子收到吉本《罗马帝国衰亡史》第二卷时流露出的那种厌倦的居高临下如出一辙：“又是一本该死的厚书！总是写写画画！是吗，吉本先生？”

Other forms of epizeuxis are less powerful. Without the rule of three, epizeuxis loses its punch. The only really great double is ‘The horror! The horror!’ in Conrad’s Heart of Darkness . Mid-sentence, the double does not do much more than add a bit of emphasis – ‘I’m shocked, shocked to find that gambling is going on in here’ – but it’s very, very rare.

其他形式的叠句效果较弱。脱离了三的规则，叠句就失去了冲击力。真正精彩的叠句只有康拉德《黑暗之心》中的“恐怖！恐怖！”。在句子中间使用叠句，除了稍加强调之外，并没有其他作用——“我震惊了，震惊地发现这里竟然在赌博”——但这种情况非常罕见。

At the beginning of a sentence epizeuxis has rather more power. ‘Tiger, tiger, burning bright’, ‘Rage, rage against the dying of the light’, ‘Gone, gone again’.

在句首，epizeuxis 具有更强的力量。“老虎，老虎，燃烧的光芒”，“怒吼，怒吼，对抗光明的消逝”，“走了，又走了”。

‘My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?’ asked Jesus on the cross. And a few years later, clearly pleased with the effect, he struck down Saul on the road to Damascus and asked, ‘Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?’, which seems an odd thing to ask of somebody that you’ve just struck down and blind, but there we are.

“我的神，我的神，为什么离弃我？”耶稣在十字架上这样问道。几年后，他显然对自己的所作所为感到满意，在大马士革的路上击倒了扫罗，问道：“扫罗，扫罗，你为什么逼迫我？”这似乎很奇怪，你刚刚击倒并弄瞎了一个人，但事实就是如此。

‘Striking down and blind’ is, by the way, an example of syllepsis.

顺便一提，“击倒并致盲”是音节修辞的一个例子。

1 From the film Fight Club (1999), surprisingly, by Chuck Palahniuk (novel) and Jim Uhls (screenplay).

1 出自电影《搏击俱乐部》（1999 年），令人惊讶的是，该片由查克·帕拉尼克（小说）和吉姆·乌尔斯（剧本）创作。

# ↩

Chapter 18

第十八章

Syllepsis

教学大纲

Syllepsis is when one word is used in two incongruous ways. In fact, it can be more than two. Let’s start with nine, which is the longest example I’ve ever found. There is an old (and doubtless untrue) story of a young journalist who was criticised by his editor for not being brief enough. His articles, he was told, had Too Many Words. The next day, he filed this report:

叠音是指一个词以两种不协调的方式使用。实际上，叠音可以不止两种。我们先来看九，这是我见过的最长的叠音例子。有个老故事（很可能是假的），讲的是一位年轻记者因为文章不够简洁而被编辑批评。编辑说他的文章“字太多了”。第二天，他提交了这样一篇报道：

A shocking affair occurred last night. Sir Edward Hopeless, as guest at Lady Panmore’s ball, complained of feeling ill, took a highball, his hat, his coat, his departure, no notice of his friends, a taxi, a pistol from his pocket, and finally his life. Nice chap. Regrets and all that.

昨晚发生了一件令人震惊的事。爱德华·霍普勒斯爵士作为潘莫尔夫人舞会的客人，声称自己身体不适，于是喝了一杯高球酒，脱下帽子和外套，悄悄离开，没有通知朋友们，叫了辆出租车，从口袋里掏出一把手枪，最后结束了自己的生命。真是个好人。事后想想，真是令人惋惜。

The verb took is applied to nine different nouns in a way that seems rather absurd. We all take no notice of things, and sometimes we take taxis, and occasionally we take our own lives, but generally in English we don’t do them in one sentence. It makes the word took look rather silly. Or rather it makes us think about the many ways that we can use the verb. It also sounds rather funny when a noun as commonplace as hat is, by grammar, made equal with a noun like life .

动词 took 可以搭配九个不同的名词，这种用法看起来相当荒谬。我们有时会对某些事情视而不见，有时我们会打车，偶尔也会自杀，但通常英语里我们不会把这些事情放在同一个句子中。这让 took 这个词显得有些滑稽。或者更确切地说，它让我们思考这个动词的多种用法。当像 hat 这样常见的名词，因为语法规则而被赋予了与 life 这样重要的名词同等的地位时，听起来也相当滑稽。

In its simplest form syllepsis is just a pun. There’s a story that Dorothy Parker once commented on her small apartment, saying: ‘I’ve barely room enough to lay my hat and a few friends.’

音节（syllepsis）最简单的形式就是一种双关语。据说多萝西·帕克曾评论过她的小公寓，她说：“我几乎连放下帽子和几个朋友的地方都挤不下。”

There are all sorts of slightly different ways that syllepsis can work. There’s a wonderful thing called a phrasal verb. Essentially it’s a verb plus a preposition, which together give you a whole new meaning: for example, doing up a house . A foreigner learning English might know the word do and the word up , but would still be unable to work out why you were performing a building skywards . And when he discovered that you could also do in your enemies, he would be done for .

音节的运用方式多种多样，略有不同。其中有一种奇妙的词组动词。它本质上是一个动词加上一个介词，组合起来就赋予了它全新的含义：例如，“doing up a house”（装修房子）。一个正在学习英语的外国人可能知道“do”和“up”这两个词，但仍然无法理解你为什么要把房子“doing up”到天上去。而当他发现你还可以用这个词来“do in your enemy”（干掉你的敌人）时，他就彻底懵了。

‘Muck out’ means to clean a stable, ‘muck in’ to help, to ‘muck about’ is to play uselessly and to ‘muck up’ is to ruin. So a lazy and incompetent stable hand could be said to muck about constantly, out and in rarely, and up everything. It’s on this principle that Rosamond Lehmann complained of her fellow novelist Ian Fleming: ‘The trouble with Ian is that he gets off with women because he can’t get on with them.’

“muck out”指的是清理马厩，“muck in”指的是帮忙，“muck about”指的是无所事事地玩耍，“muck up”指的是搞砸。所以，一个懒惰无能的马夫可以说总是无所事事，很少出去或进来，而且总是把一切都搞砸。正是基于这个原则，罗莎蒙德·莱曼抱怨她的同行小说家伊恩·弗莱明说：“伊恩的问题在于，他能和女人相处融洽，是因为他根本无法和她们相处。”

Or you can use the verb plain and the verb phrasal in one sentence. There’s a song called ‘Have Some Madeira M’Dear’, which contains long lines of syllepsis like ‘she made no reply, up her mind, and a dash for the door’.

或者你可以在一个句子中使用动词原形和动词短语。有一首歌叫《来点马德拉酒吧，亲爱的》，里面有很多音节很长的句子，比如“她没有回答，下定决心，然后冲向门口”。

But the commonest form is the simple contrast of the concrete and the abstract. When the prophet Joel told the people of Israel to ‘Rend your heart, and not your garments’ he was using the same trick that the prophet Mick Jagger 1 employed when he talked in one song about a lady who was able to blow not only his nose, but his mind, although for rather different purposes. Indeed, one suspects that Mr Jagger was planning another syllepsis based on blow that would have got the song banned on radio.

但最常见的形式是具体与抽象的简单对比。先知约珥告诉以色列人“撕裂你们的心，不要撕裂你们的衣服”，他用的技巧和先知米克·贾格尔在一首歌里提到的技巧如出一辙。贾格尔在歌里唱到一位女士不仅能帮他擤鼻涕，还能帮他擤脑子，尽管目的截然不同。事实上，人们怀疑贾格尔先生原本打算用另一个以“blow”（擤鼻涕）为主题的音节，那样的话，这首歌肯定会被电台禁播。

There’s something ridiculous about syllepsis, which is probably what attracted Lewis Carroll to it. Lines like:

音节重复这种修辞手法本身就有点荒诞，这大概就是它吸引刘易斯·卡罗尔的地方。比如这样的句子：

You may seek it with thimbles – and seek it with care;

你可以用顶针去寻找它——并且要小心翼翼地去寻找；

You may hunt it with forks and hope;

你可以用叉子和希望去猎捕它；

You may threaten its life with a railway-share;

你可能会用铁路股份威胁到它的生命；

You may charm it with smiles and soap.

你可以用微笑和肥皂来讨它欢心。

It can also make you look very clever (usually while it makes others look ridiculous). Syllepsis was a favourite of the poet Alexander Pope. He loved combining the abstract with the concrete to make others look silly. A girl might ‘Lose her heart or honour at a ball’ or ‘Stain her honour or her new brocade’. He even used it to make fun of Queen Anne:

它还能让你显得非常聪明（通常会让别人显得滑稽可笑）。双关语是诗人亚历山大·蒲柏最喜欢的修辞手法之一。他喜欢将抽象与具象结合起来，使别人显得愚蠢。比如，一个女孩可能会“在舞会上失去她的心或名誉”，或者“玷污了她的名誉或新锦缎”。他甚至用这种修辞手法来嘲讽安妮女王：

Here Thou, great Anna! whom three Realms obey,

伟大的安娜啊！三界臣服于你！

Dost sometimes Counsel take – and sometimes Tea.

有时候，Dost会听取建议，有时候会喝茶。

(It should be noted that, when Pope wrote that, tea was pronounced tay and rhymed with obey .) Syllepsis was also a favourite of Charles Dickens, who wrote lines like: ‘Mr Pickwick took his hat and his leave’, or ‘He fell into a barrow, and fast asleep’. Indeed, for my money, Dickens wrote the most splendid syllepsis in England with: ‘Miss Bolo rose from the table considerably agitated, and went straight home, in a flood of tears, and a sedan chair.’

（值得注意的是，蒲柏写下这段话时，“tea”的发音是“tay”，与“obey”押韵。）双关语也是查尔斯·狄更斯钟爱的修辞手法，他曾写过诸如“匹克威克先生摘下帽子告辞”或“他跌进手推车里，很快就睡着了”之类的句子。事实上，在我看来，狄更斯在英国写出了最精彩的双关语：“博洛小姐激动地从桌边站起来，泪流满面地坐上轿子，径直回家去了。”

But the advantages of syllepsis are also its failings. Syllepsis makes the reader astonished and go back to check what the word was and how it’s working now. It’s terribly witty, but it’s terribly witty in a look-at-me-aren’t-I-witty sort of way. There’s a sense in which it’s a cheap thrill. When Alanis Morissette sings ‘You held your breath and the door for me’ 2 you can either marvel at her rhetorical deftness or turn up your nose and off the radio. Syllepsis can get out of hand, up your nose, on your nerves and used too much.

但双关语的优点也正是它的缺点。双关语会让读者感到惊讶，并回头去查证刚才的词是什么，以及它现在是如何发挥作用的。它确实很机智，但这种机智却是一种“看我多机智”式的炫技。某种程度上，它是一种廉价的刺激。当艾拉妮丝·莫莉塞特唱到“你为我屏住呼吸，关上门”时，你可以惊叹于她修辞的精妙，也可以嗤之以鼻，关掉收音机。双关语一旦滥用，就会让人反感、烦躁，甚至被过度使用。

There are, though, subtle syllepses. ‘Make love not war’ is a syllepsis, just one that’s barely noticeable. It gives the phrase its spice, but you wouldn’t be able to pick out the flavour without a good long chew. The same goes in a sense for ‘Tea and Sympathy’ or the two boys in Tom Sawyer who ‘covered themselves in dust and glory’. These tiny syllepses hide all over the place. The reader likes the line, remembers the line, but doesn’t know why.

然而，其中也存在一些微妙的音节。“Make love not war”（要做爱，不要战争）就是一个音节，只不过它几乎难以察觉。它赋予了这句话独特的韵味，但你若不仔细品味，恐怕难以察觉。从某种意义上说，“Tea and Sympathy”（茶与同情）或《汤姆·索亚历险记》中那两个“浑身沾满尘土和荣耀”的男孩也是如此。这些细微的音节隐藏在字里行间。读者喜欢这句诗，记住这句诗，却说不出个所以然。

Nobody seriously believes that aviaries anger an omnipotent and ferocious being. If we did believe that, we wouldn’t have aviaries. It’s an insane thought. Nonetheless, William Blake is still in print saying:

没人会真的相信鸟舍会触怒全能而凶猛的神灵。如果我们真这么认为，就不会建鸟舍了。这简直是荒谬的想法。然而，威廉·布莱克至今仍在印刷出版，上面写着：

A robin redbreast in a cage

笼子里的知更鸟

Puts all Heaven in a rage.

激怒了整个天堂。

Why? Because the third stressed syllable of each line is ‘in’. The first time, the in is physical, the second time it is abstract. And the result is a couplet with no theological or logical backing, which has nonetheless survived for hundreds of years. The subtle disorientation of the syllepsis, and the neatness of the rhyme, makes us believe in something that we would scoff at were it phrased in any other way by any other animal rights activist.

为什么？因为每行诗句的第三个重读音节都是“in”。第一次出现时，“in”是实物，第二次出现时则是抽象概念。结果就形成了一首没有任何神学或逻辑支撑的对句，却流传了数百年之久。这种音节排列的微妙错位，以及押韵的巧妙，让我们相信了某些东西——如果换成其他动物权利活动家用其他方式表达，我们肯定会嗤之以鼻。

Somewhere in a Californian hotel there are, according to the Eagles, mirrors on the ceiling . There is also pink champagne on ice. The first on is the normal attached to , the second is a special colloquial usage. It’s like being ‘out of your mind and out of a job’, but so much softer. There’s just enough of a shift to prick the listener’s ears up. If the line had been ‘Mirrors on the ceiling and champagne on the bar’ it wouldn’t be half as memorable. But it would still be a good example of isocolon.

据老鹰乐队所言，加州某家酒店的天花板上装着镜子，冰镇着粉红香槟。第一个“on”是通常的用法，第二个“on”则是特殊的口语用法。这就像“神志不清又失业”一样，但语气要柔和得多。这种细微的语调变化足以引起听众的注意。如果歌词是“天花板上的镜子和吧台上的香槟”，那就远没有现在这么令人印象深刻了。但它仍然是等长句的一个很好的例子。

1 The song – ‘Honky Tonk Women’ – is credited to Jagger/Richards.

1 这首歌——《Honky Tonk Women》——的作者是 Jagger/Richards。

2 ‘Head Over Feet’ (1996) by Alanis Morissette and Glen Ballard.

2 《Head Over Feet》（1996 年），艾拉妮丝·莫莉塞特和格伦·巴拉德演唱。

# ↩

Chapter 19

第十九章

Isocolon

等结肠

Roses are red.

玫瑰是红色的。

Violets are blue.

紫罗兰是蓝色的。

That, at its simplest, is isocolon. Two clauses that are grammatically parallel, two sentences that are structurally the same. The Ancient Greeks were rather obsessed with isocolon, the modern world has rather forgotten it. The Greeks loved the sense of balance that it gave to writing, which reflected the sense of balance that they admired in thought. With isocolon one seems reasonable; without isocolon one seems hasty. With isocolon language acquired a calm rhythm, without isocolon prose became a formless heap. On the one hand the figure could describe antithesis with its graceful contrasts, on the other hand the trick could show emphasis through its gentle repetitions. O for the classical balance! Woe to the modern mess!

简而言之，这就是等距句。两个语法平行的分句，两个结构相同的句子。古希腊人对等距句颇为痴迷，而现代世界却几乎将其遗忘。希腊人喜爱它赋予文字的平衡感，这反映了他们思想中崇尚的平衡。有了等距句，文字显得合情合理；没有等距句，文字则显得仓促。有了等距句，语言便拥有了沉稳的节奏；没有等距句，散文便沦为一堆杂乱无章的堆砌物。一方面，这种修辞手法以其优美的对比来描绘对立；另一方面，它又能通过巧妙的重复来强调重点。啊，古典的平衡！唉，现代的混乱！

Because though isocolon can still be used in the calm Greek manner, it usually isn’t. When Cassius Clay said ‘Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee’, he had no calm and peaceful thoughts in his mind. And when Rick tells Ilsa, ‘Where I’m going, you can’t follow. What I’ve got to do, you can’t be any part of’, he doesn’t sound like Socrates contemplating virtue, he sounds like a man in a crisis with a gun and a girl at an airport.

虽然等长句仍然可以以希腊人那种平静的方式使用，但通常并非如此。当卡修斯·克莱说“像蝴蝶一样轻盈，像蜜蜂一样蜇人”时，他心中绝无平静祥和之意。而当里克对伊尔莎说“我要去的地方，你不能跟随。我要做的事，你不能参与”时，他听起来不像苏格拉底在思考美德，而像一个在机场遇到危机、手里拿着枪、身边还带着女孩的男人。

Modern isocolons tend to work as a kind of spot-the-difference game. We use the similarities to point up the differences, and use the differences to point up the similarities. Rick’s lines contrast where with what , going with doing , following with taking part. So the sentences are differentiated: the first is about geographical movement, the second is about physical action. But at the same time the sentences simply restate each other. The ‘I’ and the ‘you can’t’ remain in their places, and Rick and Ilsa part at the airport.

现代的等长句往往像是一种“找不同”游戏。我们利用相似之处来指出不同之处，又利用不同之处来指出相似之处。里克的句子对比了“哪里”和“什么”、“去”和“做”、“跟随”和“参与”。因此，这些句子是有区别的：第一个句子描述的是地理上的移动，第二个句子描述的是实际的动作。但与此同时，这些句子又互相重复。“我”和“你不能”的位置保持不变，里克和伊尔莎在机场告别。

Similarity and difference, comparison and contrast, are the stock in trade of isocolon, and that’s how Shakespeare liked to use it. When Brutus is explaining why he killed Julius Caesar, he gives this reply:

相似与差异、比较与对比是等长句的惯用手法，莎士比亚也喜欢这样运用它。当布鲁图斯解释他为何刺杀尤利乌斯·凯撒时，他是这样回答的：

As Caesar loved me, I weep for him; as he was fortunate, I rejoice at it; as he was valiant, I honour him: but, as he was ambitious, I slew him. There is tears for his love; joy for his fortune; honour for his valour; and death for his ambition.

凯撒爱我，我为他哭泣；他幸运，我为此欢欣；他英勇，我敬重；但他野心勃勃，我杀了他。我为他的爱流泪；为他的幸运欢欣；为他的英勇敬重；为他的野心而死。

This is obviously a much more extended case of isocolon. You don’t have to stop at two parallels, you can go on for a very long time, so long as your lungs are big enough. John F. Kennedy in his inauguration address announced:

这显然是一个持续时间更长的等结肠病例。你不必止步于两个平行线，只要你的肺足够大，你可以一直呼吸下去。约翰·F·肯尼迪在他的就职演说中宣布：

Let every nation know, whether it wishes us well or ill, that we shall pay any price, bear any burden, meet any hardship, support any friend, oppose any foe, to assure the survival and the success of liberty.

让所有国家都知道，无论他们对我们抱有善意还是恶意，为了确保自由的生存和胜利，我们将付出任何代价，承受任何负担，克服任何困难，支持任何朋友，反对任何敌人。

And Winston Churchill beat that with the slightly ridiculous:

而温斯顿·丘吉尔则用一句略显荒谬的话驳斥了这种说法：

Fill the armies, rule the air, pour out the munitions, strangle the U-boats, sweep the mines, plough the land, build the ships, guard the streets, succour the wounded, uplift the downcast, and honour the brave.

充实军队，称霸制空，倾泻弹药，扼杀潜艇，扫除水雷，耕耘土地，建造舰船，守卫街道，救助伤员，鼓舞沮丧者，表彰勇士。

This also shows up isocolon’s weakness: people can hear it happening and it can all start to sound rather forced and artificial. Silly even. It’s very hard to work an extended isocolon in subtly. It’s strictly for the moment when you’re addressing the crowds in Rome or Washington, or trying to win the Second World War over the radio. It’s not the sort of trick you can use down the pub or try over dinner. If you do, Shakespeare makes fun of you thus:

这也暴露了等长句的弱点：人们能听出来，而且听起来会很生硬做作，甚至有点傻。要巧妙地运用等长句非常困难。它只适用于你在罗马或华盛顿向人群发表演讲，或者试图通过广播赢得第二次世界大战的情况。这不是那种你可以在酒吧里或餐桌上用的技巧。如果你这么做了，莎士比亚会这样嘲笑你：

I praise God for you, sir: your reasons at dinner have been sharp and sententious; pleasant without scurrility, witty without affection, audacious without impudency, learned without opinion, and strange without heresy.

先生，我感谢上帝赐予您：您在晚餐上的发言尖锐而精辟；既令人愉快又不粗俗，既诙谐又不矫情，既大胆又不厚颜无耻，既博学又不固执己见，既奇特又不离经叛道。

Much better to keep isocolons short and snappy. Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee, chat like a human being. Thus you can keep to the twin powers of isocolon: antitheses like ‘Marry in haste, repent at leisure’; and restatements like ‘Thy kingdom come, thy will be done’.

最好让等长句简洁明了。像蝴蝶一样轻盈，像蜜蜂一样蜇人，像人一样健谈。这样你就能充分发挥等长句的双重作用：既能表达对比，例如“仓促结婚，慢慢后悔”；又能表达重申，例如“愿你的国降临，愿你的旨意成就”。

The isocolon is particularly useful to advertisers. The parallelism can imply that two statements are the same thing even if they aren’t. ‘Have a break. Have a Kit-Kat’ is a clever little line because it uses isocolon to try to make two rather different things synonymous. The same goes for ‘The future’s bright. The future’s Orange’.

等长冒号对广告商来说尤其有用。平行结构可以暗示两个陈述句意思相同，即使它们并非如此。“休息一下，吃块奇巧巧克力”就是一句巧妙的广告语，因为它运用了等长冒号，试图将两个截然不同的事物等同起来。同样的道理也适用于“未来一片光明，未来一片橙色”。

Isocolon is also littered throughout the lyrics of pop music and the words of hymns.

等长句也大量出现在流行音乐的歌词和赞美诗的歌词中。

Morning has broken, like the first morning.

晨光破晓，如同第一个清晨。

Blackbird has spoken, like the first bird.

黑鸟发声了，就像第一只鸟一样。

Melodies tend to repeat themselves, and so the words that are sung over them repeat themselves too. Sometimes these lines even conform to the ultra-strict definition of isocolon in the Rhetorica ad Herennium : 1 that the two clauses have exactly the same number of syllables.

旋律往往会重复，因此与之相配的歌词也会重复。有时，这些歌词甚至符合《致赫伦尼乌斯修辞学》中对等长句的极其严格的定义：即两个分句的音节数完全相同。

But mostly our isocolons are heard, not counted; sensed, not defined. It is the wit of Churchill describing Field Marshal Montgomery as ‘In defeat, unbeatable; in victory, unbearable’. Or it’s the finality of ‘Ashes to ashes, dust to dust’. Or it’s the simplicity of ‘You pays your money and you takes your choice’.

但我们的同位素大多是被听见，而非被计数；是被感知，而非被定义。这体现在丘吉尔对蒙哥马利元帅的妙语描述中：“战败时，所向披靡；胜利时，所令人难以忍受”。又或是“尘归尘，土归土”的终结性。再或是“你付钱，你做主”的简洁明了。

Which is also an example of enallage.

这也是 enallage 的一个例子。

1 The Rhetorica ad Herennium is the standard classical work on rhetoric, and contains all the strictest definitions. But see Epilogue, p. 203 .

1 《致赫伦尼乌斯的修辞学》是古典修辞学的标准著作，包含了所有最严格的定义。但参见第203页的后记。

# ↩

Chapter 20

第二十章

Enallage

填充

Enallage (e-NALL-aj-ee) is a deliberate grammatical mistake. That definition raises all sorts of philosophical questions about whether a mistake can be deliberate, and all sorts of linguistic questions about what correct English grammar is and whether one chap ever really has the right to tell another chap he’s wrong. So perhaps it would be better to say that enallage is when a phrase stands out because of its unusual grammar. Simples.

Enallage（发音为 e-NALL-aj-ee）是一种故意的语法错误。这个定义引发了一系列哲学问题，例如错误是否可以是故意的；也引发了一系列语言学问题，例如正确的英语语法是什么，以及一个人是否真的有权指出另一个人的错误。所以，或许更准确的说法是，enallage 指的是某个短语因为其不寻常的语法而显得格外引人注目。就这么简单。

At the end of Heart of Darkness , as they sail slowly back down the mysterious river …

在《黑暗之心》的结尾，当他们缓缓乘船沿神秘的河流返回时……

… the manager’s boy put his insolent black head in the doorway, and said in a tone of scathing contempt—

经理的助手把那颗傲慢的黑脑袋伸进门口，用一种充满轻蔑的语气说道——

‘Mistah Kurtz – he dead.’

“米斯塔·库尔茨——他死了。”

Joseph Conrad knew that grammatically a verb was required to make a complete sentence, but the line ‘Mr Kurtz is dead’ would have been neither striking nor memorable. It wouldn’t have made the dictionary of quotations and T.S. Eliot wouldn’t have used it as the epigraph for ‘The Hollow Men’. Heart of Darkness is 39,000 words long, but everybody remembers those four. It’s the bad grammar what makes the phrase. That enallage.

约瑟夫·康拉德知道，从语法上讲，一个完整的句子需要一个动词，但“库尔茨先生死了”这句话既不引人注目，也不令人难忘。它不会被收入引语词典，T·S·艾略特也不会把它用作《空心人》的题词。《黑暗之心》长达39000字，但每个人都记得这四个字。正是这糟糕的语法造就了这句话。这句引语。

But though Conrad, the novelist, may make his mistakes intentionally, Joe Jacobs, the boxing manager, probably did not. He made the dictionary of quotations 1 with an angry enallage. After his boxer Max Schmeling lost on points, Jacobs shouted to anybody who would listen that ‘We was robbed’. Had his grammar been any better, Mr Jacobs would be forgotten.

虽然小说家康拉德可能故意犯错，但拳击经纪人乔·雅各布斯很可能并非如此。他用一句愤怒的引语为引语词典增添了浓墨重彩的一笔。他的拳击手马克斯·施梅林点数落败后，雅各布斯对着所有愿意听的人大喊：“我们被黑了！” 如果他语法好一点，雅各布斯先生恐怕早已被人遗忘。

And sometimes it is a little hard to say whether the enallage was deliberate or not. T.S. Eliot certainly knew the English language. He knew that we means you and I and that us means you and me . But he still started ‘The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock’ 2 with the words:

有时很难说这种拼贴是刻意为之还是无心之举。T·S·艾略特当然精通英语。他知道“we”指“你和我”，“us”指“你和我”。但他仍然以这样的歌词作为《J·阿尔弗雷德·普鲁弗洛克的情歌》的开头：

Let us go then, you and I,

那我们走吧，你和我。

Let I go?

放我走？

Of course, it may just have been there to rhyme with sky in the next line. I’ll never be sure and I can’t ask him now. Most people don’t notice the problem. But I have a theory that it’s that little enallage, pricking away at the unconscious, that has made the line so famous.

当然，也许只是为了和下一句的“sky”押韵。我永远也无法确定，现在也没法问他。大多数人都没注意到这个问题。但我有个理论，正是这小小的押韵，潜移默化地触动着人们的潜意识，才让这句诗如此出名。

Or maybe it was just the rhyme. After all, Shakespeare did it, using the same substitution.

或许只是押韵而已。毕竟，莎士比亚也用过同样的替换手法。

Unless you would devise some virtuous lie,

除非你能编造出一个合情合理的谎言，

To do more for me than mine own desert,

为我做的，不仅仅是我自己的沙漠，

And hang more praise upon deceased I

并把更多的赞美归于已故的我

Than niggard truth would willingly impart:

比吝啬的真相更愿意透露：

And nobody says Shakespeare couldn’t write.

谁也说莎士比亚不会写作。

Strict grammarians don’t seem to mind about the line ‘Love me tender’ either. Any child could tell you that the words should be ‘love me tenderly, love me truly’, but they aren’t and it’s much better that way. The chap who wrote those lyrics, Ken Darby, had the tune to contend with. It’s an old Civil War melody that was originally about a girl called Aura Lea, and Darby had to make his lines fit. Tenderly and truly would have added another note to the end of the tune. If this was what happened, then, just as Eliot could point at Shakespeare, Darby could finger Dylan Thomas’ ‘Do not go gentle into that good night’ or Alexander Pope’s ‘Hope springs eternal in the human breast’. In both cases the poor poets were just trying to fit their thoughts into verse, and if that meant they had to drop a ‘ly’, then so be it.

严谨的语法学家似乎也不在意“温柔地爱我”这句歌词。任何一个孩子都能告诉你，歌词应该是“温柔地爱我，真诚地爱我”，但事实并非如此，而且这样更好。创作这句歌词的肯·达比（Ken Darby）当时还得考虑曲调。这是一首古老的南北战争时期的民谣，最初是关于一个名叫奥拉·莉亚（Aura Lea）的女孩的，达比必须让他的歌词与曲调相符。“温柔地爱我，真诚地爱我”会在曲调末尾增加一个音符。如果真是这样，那么就像艾略特可以引用莎士比亚的作品一样，达比也可以引用狄兰·托马斯的“不要温和地走进那个良夜”或亚历山大·蒲柏的“希望永存于人心”。在这两种情况下，可怜的诗人只是试图将他们的想法融入诗歌，如果这意味着他们必须去掉一个“ly”，那就这样吧。

1 Bartlett’s Familiar Quotations .

1 巴特利特的名言警句。

2 From Collected Poems 1909–1962 by T.S. Eliot, published by Faber and Faber Ltd.

2 选自 T.S. Eliot 的《诗集 1909–1962》，由 Faber and Faber Ltd. 出版。

# ↩

Chapter 21

第21章

A Divagation Concerning Versification

关于韵律化的分歧

English verse is a reasonably simple business. Each English word has a stress on it. When a beggar starts work, he needs to begin beggin’. Begin has the stress on the second syllable – beGIN – and beggin’ has the stress on the first – BEGgin’. The same thing goes with the verb to rebel and the noun a rebel . A REBel ReBELS. When you give a gift, you preSENT a PREsent. The only difference between the words is the stress.

英语诗歌其实相当简单。每个英语单词都有重音。乞丐开始工作时，他需要开始乞讨。begin 的重音在第二个音节——beGIN——而 beggin’ 的重音在第一个音节——BEGgin’。动词 rebel 和名词 a rebel 也是如此。a rebel 反叛。送礼物时，你送的是 present 礼物。这两个词唯一的区别就是重音。

Every word in English has a particular stress, and when a foreigner gets it wrong we notice, and we snigger. There’s an old joke with many variations all of which involve a Frenchman in pursuit of a penis, rather than happiness. That’s partially because the French don’t pronounce their Hs, but mainly because HAPPiness and a PENis are stressed differently.

英语里每个单词都有特定的重音，外国人要是发错音，我们就会注意到，还会偷笑。有个老笑话有很多版本，都讲的是一个法国人追求的是阴茎（penis），而不是幸福（happiness）。这部分是因为法国人发“h”音不发，但主要原因是“幸福”（happyiness）和“阴茎”（penis）的重音不一样。

Some words even get two stresses. Antidote goes TUM-te-TUM. UNDerSTANDing goes TUM-te-TUM-te. And sometimes the stress is optional. You usually say HAPPiness, but you can, if you like, say HAPPinESS.

有些词甚至有两个重音。Antidote 的重音是 TUM-te-TUM。UNDerSTANDing 的重音是 TUM-te-TUM-te。有时重音是可选的。通常你会说 HAPPiness，但如果你愿意，也可以说 HAPPinESS。

Also, even when a sentence is made out of words of one syllable, some will be stressed and some won’t. ‘A cup of tea’ will always be stressed ‘a CUP of TEA’. (Unless, I suppose, you’re asked whether you wanted two cups next to tea, in which case you might reply, ‘No, I want A cup OF tea’.)

此外，即使句子由单音节词组成，有些词会重读，有些则不会。“一杯茶”的重音永远是“一杯茶”。（除非，我想，别人问你是不是要两杯茶，在这种情况下，你可能会回答：“不，我要一杯茶。”）

So ‘a lovely cup of tea’ goes te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM. ‘I want a lovely cup of tea’ goes te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM. ‘I really want a lovely cup of tea’ goes te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM. And now you’ve got a rhythm going.

所以，“一杯好茶”的节奏是 te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM。“我想要一杯好茶”的节奏是 te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM。“我真的想要一杯好茶”的节奏是 te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM。现在你已经掌握节奏了。

‘Compare’ is a te-TUM. ‘Summer’ is a TUM-te. So ‘Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day’ goes te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM. And the next line, ‘Thou art more lovely and more temperate’, goes exactly the same way. ‘Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May’ is the same. ‘And summer’s lease hath all too short a date’ is the same. Five te-TUMS in a row. Try reading those lines out while tapping your finger on something to keep time.

“Compare”是 te-TUM。“Summer”是 TUM-te。所以，“Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day”的发音是 te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM-te-TUM。下一句，“Thou art more lovely and more temperate”的发音也完全一样。“Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May”也是如此。“And summer’s lease hath all too short a date”也一样。连续五个 te-TUMS。试着一边用手指敲击东西打拍子，一边读这些诗句。

In verse a te-TUM is called an iamb, and five in a row is called a pentameter (that’s the same pent as pentagon). So five te-TUMs are called an iambic pentameter.

在诗歌中，一个 te-TUM 音步被称为抑扬格，五个 te-TUM 音步连在一起被称为五音步（pentameter，其中 pent 与 pentagon 的发音相同）。因此，五个 te-TUM 音步被称为抑扬格五音步。

Of course, there are lots of other ways that you can write. The iamb is just one of the four basic feet:

当然，还有很多其他的写作方式。抑扬格只是四种基本音步之一：

Iamb – te-TUM

Iamb – te-TUM

Trochee – TUMty

扬子 - TUMty

Anapaest – te-te-TUM

Anapaest – te-te-TUM

Dactyl – TUM-te-ty

指节 – TUM-te-ty

And the pentameter is one of the three basic meters:

五音步是三种基本韵律之一：

Pentameter – five in a row

五音步——连续五个音步

Tetrameter – four in a row

四音步诗——连续四个音步

Trimeter – three in a row

三音步——连续三个

So you can pick one from each list, and you’ve got yourself a verse form. Choose anapaest and tetrameter and you’ve got:

所以你可以从每个列表中选择一个，这样你就得到了一种诗歌形式。选择抑扬格和四音步，你就得到了：

te-te-TUM te-te-TUM te-te-TUM te-te-TUM

肚子 肚子 肚子 肚子 肚子

Which Byron used for:

拜伦用它做什么：

The As syr ian came down like a wolf on the fold

亚述人像狼扑向羊圈一样冲了过来。

And his co horts were gleam ing in purp le and gold

他的同僚们身着紫金色的华服，熠熠生辉。

There are only twelve combinations, and they’ve all been tried a few times. And people have even gone off into the more obscure feet and lengths. Obviously the meters don’t have to be just three, four and five. You can do anything from one up to infinity, if you feel like it. And there are all sorts of other strange feet like the choriamb (TUM-te-te-TUM) and the molossus (TUM! TUM! TUM!). But these strange ones have never really worked well in English apart from the amphibrach (te-TUM-te), which is the basis of the limerick:

只有十二种组合，而且每一种都尝试过好几次。人们甚至还探索过一些更冷门的音步和长度。显然，韵律并不一定非得是三、四、五。如果你愿意，你可以用从一到无穷大的任何数量。还有各种其他奇特的音步，比如抑扬格（TUM-te-te-TUM）和莫洛苏斯（TUM! TUM! TUM!）。但除了双音步（te-TUM-te）——五行打油诗的基础——之外，这些奇特的音步在英语中从未真正流行起来：

There was a young man from Cal cutt a

有个来自加尔各答的年轻人

But I digress. The point is that even with the basic feet and the basic meters there are still only two or three combinations that actually get a lot of use. Anapaests and dactyls tend to sound a bit silly. Byron made the anapaest serious, but that’s because he was an absolutely bloody amazing poet. If you try it yourself you’ll probably end up with something that sounds like a nursery rhyme, because anapaests and dactyls are the nursery rhyme feet and they tend to sound rather higgledy piggledy wiggledy woo. ‘Little Miss Muffet, she sat on a tuffet …’

但我跑题了。重点是，即使有了基本的音步和韵律，真正常用的组合也只有两三种。抑扬格和扬抑格听起来往往有点滑稽。拜伦让抑扬格变得严肃起来，但这完全是因为他是一位才华横溢的诗人。如果你自己尝试，最终可能会写出一首听起来像童谣的作品，因为抑扬格和扬抑格正是童谣的音步，听起来往往杂乱无章，像是“小猪咩咩叫”。比如，“小玛菲特小姐，她坐在小凳子上……”

The trochee doesn’t sound silly, but it does sound a bit like a hammer, banging away. So Henry Wadsworth Longfellow’s 1855 poem, The Song of Hiawatha , which is all in trochees, goes like this:

扬抑格听起来并不滑稽，但确实有点像锤子敲击的声音。亨利·沃兹沃思·朗费罗1855年创作的诗歌《海华沙之歌》全部采用扬抑格写成，歌词如下：

By the shores of Gitche Gumee,

在吉切古米湖畔，

By the shining Big-Sea-Water,

在波光粼粼的大海水边，

Stood the wigwam of Nokomis,

诺科米斯的圆锥形帐篷矗立在那里，

Daughter of the Moon, Nokomis.

月亮之女，诺科米斯。

Dark behind it rose the forest,

黑暗中，森林在其后升起。

Rose the black and gloomy pine-trees,

玫瑰照亮了那些阴暗的黑松树，

Rose the firs with cones upon them;

松树上挂满了球果；

Bright before it beat the water,

在击打水面之前，它闪闪发光。

Beat the clear and sunny water,

战胜清澈阳光下的水，

Beat the shining Big-Sea-Water.

战胜闪耀的大海水。

I mean it’s effective. But it’s a bit obvious. And remember that Hiawatha is an epic poem. After a while it feels as though there are builders working in your head.

我的意思是，它的确有效，但有点显而易见。而且别忘了，《海华沙之歌》是一部史诗。听多了，你会感觉好像有建筑工人在你的脑子里忙碌着。

Hiawatha actually made the trochee fashionable, something that doesn’t ordinarily happen to metrical units. In November 1855 the gossip column of the New York Times claimed: ‘The madness of the hour takes the metrical shape of trochees, everybody writes trochaics, talks trochaics, and thinks in trochees’, which would drive me mad. Mind you, it’s possible that everybody was talking in trochees. It’s insanely simple once you get the rhythm in your head. Most people can improvise in unrhymed dactyls for hours. It’s just that you lose all your friends if you do.

海华沙实际上让扬抑格流行起来，这在韵律单位中并不常见。1855年11月，《纽约时报》的八卦专栏宣称：“当下的疯狂以扬抑格的韵律形式呈现，人人都用扬抑格写作、说话、思考”，这简直要把我逼疯了。不过，也许当时每个人都在用扬抑格说话。一旦你掌握了节奏，它就极其简单。大多数人都能即兴创作几个小时的无韵抑扬格诗。只不过，如果你这么做，你会失去所有朋友。

And that, as the bishop remarked to the crocodile, leaves us with only one foot: the iamb. The soft and lovely iamb. The humble te-TUM. Because the TUM falls on the offbeat, as it were, the rhythm is gentler. It never has the primeval power of the trochee, but nor does it have any of its primeval coarseness. The iamb is just the gentle rhythm, the waves lapping in the background.

正如主教对鳄鱼所说，这让我们只剩下一只脚：抑扬格。柔和优美的抑扬格。谦逊的“te-TUM”。因为“tum”落在弱拍上，节奏更加柔和。它没有扬抑格那种原始的力量，也没有扬抑格那种原始的粗犷。抑扬格就是轻柔的节奏，如同背景中轻柔的波浪拍打着海岸。

The only question that remains is how many? The simplest answer is the greedy one. Four and three alternating: the tetrameter and the trimeter. This is called the ballad meter and it sounds wonderfully traditional.

剩下的唯一问题就是：多少个音步？最简单的答案就是最直接的答案：四音步和三音步交替。这被称为民谣韵律，听起来非常传统。

There is a house in New Orl eans

新奥尔良有一栋房子

They call The Ris ing Sun

他们称旭日为“旭日”。

It’s been the ruin of man y a poor boy

它毁掉了许多穷男孩。

In God , I know I’m one .

在上帝面前，我知道我是一体的。

You probably noticed that the third line there isn’t quite right. There are three soft syllables between man- and boy . That’s all right for two reasons. First, there’s slurring. Many a can be pronounced as men-yer . Give it a go. Men-yer poor boy . So that brings it down to only two soft syllables. What’s poor doing there? Well, the truth is that once you’ve established a rhythm you can vary it a bit. It even makes the ballad meter sound more traditional. Rather like wonky timbers on an old building. They look good, and as long as it’s all structurally sound, the more wonk the better. Here’s the opening of The Rime of the Ancient Mariner :

你可能已经注意到第三行不太对劲。man- 和 boy 之间有三个轻柔的音节。这没关系，原因有二。首先，这里可以连读。很多 a 都可以读作 men-yer。试试看。Men-yer poor boy。这样就只剩下两个轻柔的音节了。poor 这个词在这里有什么用呢？其实，一旦你确定了节奏，就可以稍微改变一下。这甚至会让民谣的韵律听起来更传统。就像老建筑上歪斜的木梁一样。它们看起来不错，只要结构稳固，越歪斜越好。以下是《古舟子咏》的开头：

It is an an cient Ma rin er ,

这是一位古老的航海家，

And he stop peth one of three .

他阻止了三人中的一个。

‘By thy long grey beard and glit tering eye ,

“以你长长的灰胡须和闪亮的眼睛起誓，

Now where fore stopp’st thou me ?’

你为何要阻止我？

It’s so damned folksy, and it’s those extra syllables here and there that make it seem so rough and ready. You can, of course, write in pure ballad meter, and it sounds a lot more respectable.

它太有乡土气息了，正是那些零星的音节让它显得如此粗犷随意。当然，你也可以用纯粹的民谣韵律来写，那样听起来就体面多了。

Because I could not stop for Death—

因为我无法停下来等待死神——

He kindly stopped for me—

他好心地停下来等我——

The Carriage held but just Ourselves—

马车里只有我们两个人——

And Immortality.

还有永生。

But it still has something of the nursery rhyme:

但它仍然保留着一些童谣的韵味：

‘The time has come ,’ the Wal rus said ,

“时候到了，”海象说。

‘To talk of man y things :

“要谈论很多事情：

Of shoes —and ships —and seal ing- wax —

鞋子——以及船只——以及封蜡——

Of cab ba ges —and kings —

关于卷心菜——以及国王——

And why the sea is boil ing hot —

为什么海水会沸腾起来——

And wheth er pigs have wings .’

以及猪是否长翅膀。

It can always be sung to the tune of ‘The House of the Rising Sun’ or ‘O Little Town of Bethlehem’. Nonetheless, you’ll be even more dignified if you move up to the straight iambic tetrameter: te-TUM te-TUM te-TUM te-TUM.

它总是可以用《日升之屋》或《小伯利恒》的曲调来演唱。然而，如果你采用标准的抑扬格四音步，你会显得更加庄重：te-TUM te-TUM te-TUM te-TUM。

The iambic tetrameter can do all sorts of things, but it’s best at being sad and lyrical.

抑扬格四音步可以表达各种各样的情感，但它最擅长表达悲伤和抒情。

I wand ered lone ly as a Cloud

我孤独地游荡，像一朵云

That floats on high o’er Vales and Hills ,

它漂浮在山谷和山丘之上，

When all at once I saw a crowd

突然间，我看到了一群人

A host of danc ing Daff o dils ;

一群翩翩起舞的水仙花；

Which has the same sort of feel as:

这与以下感受类似：

She walks in beaut y, like the night

她漫步在美中，如同夜晚。

Of cloud less climes and star ry skies ;

晴朗无云的气候和繁星点点的夜空；

And all that’s best of dark and bright

以及黑暗与光明的一切美好

Meet in her asp ect and her eyes :

从她的容貌和眼神中相遇：

It’s beautiful and melancholy and loving. One thing about it, though, is that it has to rhyme. There’s an odd thing about English verse that when you have an even number of feet in a line, it doesn’t seem right to pause. When you have an odd number of feet, people just naturally take a breath at the end of the line. Why this should be is a complete mystery, but it’s almost always true. Try reading this aloud:

它优美、忧伤而又充满爱意。不过，它必须押韵。英语诗歌有个奇特的规则：当一行诗的音步数为偶数时，似乎不应该停顿；而当音步数为奇数时，人们自然而然地会在行尾换气。个中缘由至今仍是个谜，但几乎总是如此。不妨试着朗读一下：

I wandered like a cloud

我像云一样飘荡。

That floats o’er vales and hills

那漂浮在山谷和丘陵之上的

And then I saw a crowd,

然后我看到了一群人，

A host of daffodils.

一大片水仙花。

Do you hear how you’re pausing? If you try tapping your finger along to the beat, you’ll find that the little pause at the end of the line is exactly one beat long. It’s as though you’re filling in the missing time and making it up to the nearest even number.

你听出你停顿的地方了吗？如果你试着用手指跟着节拍打拍子，你会发现每行末尾的短暂停顿正好是一个节拍。就好像你在填补缺失的时间，让它接近偶数一样。

The important thing here is that there are two ways of marking the end of a line. You can do it with a rhyme, or you can do it with a pause. And in the tetrameter that second option is out the window. So all tetrameters have to rhyme.

这里重要的是，有两种方式可以标记一行诗的结尾。你可以用押韵，也可以用停顿。但在四音步诗中，第二种方式行不通。所以所有四音步诗都必须押韵。

I wandered lonely as a cloud

我像云一样孤独地游荡。

That floats on high o’er vales and hills

它漂浮在高高的山谷和山丘之上

When all at once I saw a host

突然间，我看到了一位主人

Of many dancing buttercups.

许多翩翩起舞的毛茛。

Is just nonsense. Of course you can rhyme it in different ways. These ones have been alternating, but you can do the straight couplet, which makes the tetrameter a lot jauntier:

简直胡说八道。当然，你可以用不同的方式押韵。这些押韵方式是交替的，但你也可以用标准的对句，这样四音步诗听起来会轻快得多：

The grave’s a fine and private place

墓地环境优美，私密性好。

But none, I think, do there embrace.

但我认为，他们中没有人会拥抱彼此。

Or you can go the other way entirely and write in the most beautiful and most melancholy form of tetrameter: the In Memoriam stanza. Alfred Tennyson’s best friend went on holiday and died. This was a bad thing for Tennyson, but a good thing for English poetry, because Tennyson settled down to write 133 short poems about his dead chum, or one long poem in 133 sections, if you want to look at it like that. The entire thing was in iambic tetrameters and they all rhyme the same way:

或者，你也可以完全反其道而行之，用最美也最忧伤的四音步诗体——悼念诗——来创作。阿尔弗雷德·丁尼生的挚友外出度假时不幸去世。这对丁尼生来说是件坏事，但对英国诗歌来说却是一件好事，因为丁尼生开始创作133首关于他逝去好友的短诗，或者，如果你愿意的话，也可以把它看作一首分为133个部分的长诗。整首诗都采用抑扬格四音步，而且韵脚完全相同：

Dark house, by which once more I stand

阴暗的房子，我又一次站在它旁边。

Here in the long unlovely street,

在这条漫长而乏味的街道上，

Doors, where my heart was used to beat

门，我心脏曾在那里跳动

So quickly, waiting for a hand,

如此迅速，等待着伸出援手，

‘And eet eet and.’ What’s so lovely about this is that it takes four lines for the whole thing to make structural sense. If you write in couplets, it’s all over in two lines. If you write in alternating rhyme, you’re wrapping up after three. But with the In Memoriam stanza that first line doesn’t make poetic sense until you come to the last syllable of the fourth. It holds and holds, and then completes. So it’s rather unfortunate that the most famous lines from the whole poem are usually quoted out of context:

“然后 eet eet and。”这首诗的妙处在于，它用了四行才构成完整的结构。如果用对句，两行就结束了；如果用交替韵，三行就结束了。但悼念诗的这节，第一行直到第四行的最后一个音节才具有诗意。它不断延展，最终才完整。所以，这首诗中最著名的几句经常被断章取义地引用，实在令人惋惜。

I hold it true, whate’er befall;

无论发生什么，我都坚信这一点；

I feel it when I sorrow most;

我最悲伤的时候会感受到它；

’Tis better to have loved and lost

爱过又失去，总比没有好。

Than never to have loved at all.

宁愿从未爱过。

Perhaps we should pause here a moment. Perhaps you think that I’m going on about verse too much. Perhaps you think the stresses don’t matter. So to show you that what I’m saying is half true, let’s go back and rewrite that in anapaests.

或许我们应该在这里稍作停顿。或许你觉得我过于强调诗歌的韵律。或许你觉得重音无关紧要。那么，为了让你明白我说的有一半是对的，让我们回到过去，用抑扬格重写一遍。

So I know it is true that what ever be fall;

所以我知道，无论发生什么；

And I feel it when ev er I sor row the most ;

每当我最悲伤的时候，我都会感受到这一点；

That ’tis bet ter to tru ly have loved and have lost

那样，曾经真心爱过又失去，总比没有好。

Than nev er to tru ly have loved one at all .

宁愿从未真正爱过一个人。

Quite aside from some little changes in meaning, you can hear how the anapaest changes the feel of the verse. You can also see how easy it is to write verse. It’s so easy to throw in a syllable here and there to make up the rhythm. That’s why poets are so fond of words like ‘Oh’ or ‘and’. It’s not that they keep saying the word in real life, it’s just that you can throw it in anywhere. ‘And thou art dead , as young and fair ’. It’s not that Byron usually started sentences with ‘and’, he just knew the quickest way to make an iambic tetrameter. If you’re really stuck you can just repeat a word: ‘My love is like a red , red rose ’. Or, if you need to lose a syllable, you can do what Tennyson did above and change whatever to whate’er . The really cheap method is to add an ‘a-’ to the beginning of a word. The syllables, they are a-changeable.

撇开一些细微的含义变化不谈，你还能听出抑扬格是如何改变诗歌的韵律感的。你也能看出写诗是多么容易。随便加个音节就能凑出节奏，这简直太容易了。这就是为什么诗人如此钟爱“哦”或“和”这样的词。倒不是说他们在现实生活中会一直说这些词，只是因为这些词可以随意插入。“而你已逝去，依然年轻貌美”。拜伦并非总是以“和”开头，他只是知道这是构成抑扬格四音步最快捷的方法。如果你真的卡住了，你可以重复一个词：“我的爱就像一朵红红的玫瑰”。或者，如果你需要去掉一个音节，你可以像丁尼生那样，把whatever改成whate'er。最简单粗暴的方法是在词首加个“a-”。音节，它们都是可以随意改变的。

The Renaissance poet Ben Jonson said that when he wanted to write poetry, he just wrote prose and then mucked around with the word order and banged it with a verbal hammer until it fitted nicely into a verse form. Or:

文艺复兴时期的诗人本·琼森曾说过，当他想写诗时，他先写散文，然后反复调整词序，用语言的锤子敲打，直到它完美地契合诗歌的形式。或者：

Ben Jonson in Renaissance claimed

文艺复兴时期的本·琼森声称

That when a verse to write he aimed [word order mangled for rhyme]

当他要写一首诗时，他的目标是[为了押韵而打乱词序]

He wrote the whole thing down in prose;

他用散文把整件事都写下来了；

And when a meter problem rose, [ arose wouldn’t fit]

当仪表出现问题时，[出现问题不合适]

He banged it with a verbal hammer,

他用言语重锤猛击它，

With clever cut or stammer-stammer,

巧妙地切入或结结巴巴，

Until it fitted into verse [ Until because till wouldn’t work]

直到它能融入诗歌中 [因为 till 用起来不合适]

And reckoned it was none the worse.

他认为情况并不算太糟。

But Ben Jonson usually wrote in the king of English verse forms, the iambic pentameter.

但本·琼森通常用英语诗歌中最美的诗歌形式——抑扬格五音步来写作。

The iambic pentameter is the Rolls-Royce of verse forms. The others are mere unicycles, tractors, quad-bikes and rickshaws. They’re fine for some particular purpose, but the iambic pentameter can do everything. It can do tragic (‘No long er mourn for me when I am dead’ ), heroic (‘Once more un to the breach , dear friends , once more’ ), motivational (‘We few , we hap py few , we band of broth ers’), pastoral (‘There is a will ow grows as lant a brook’ ), romantic (‘If mu sic be the food of love , play on’ ), casual (‘The la dy doth pro test too much , me thinks’ ), or witty:

抑扬格五音步是诗歌形式中的劳斯莱斯。其他的诗歌形式不过是独轮车、拖拉机、四轮摩托车和人力车。它们在某些特定场合或许不错，但抑扬格五音步几乎无所不能。它可以表达悲剧（“我死后，不要再为我哀悼”）、英雄主义（“亲爱的朋友们，再次冲锋陷阵，再次”）、励志（“我们少数人，我们幸福的少数人，我们兄弟连”）、田园风情（“溪边斜生一柳”）、浪漫情怀（“如果音乐是爱情的食粮，那就继续演奏吧”）、轻松随意（“我觉得这位女士的辩解有点过头了”），或者诙谐幽默：

True wit is na ture to ad van tage dressed ,

真正的智慧是将天赋优势巧妙地运用到生活中。

What oft was thought , but ne’er so well ex pressed .

人们常常想到这一点，但从未如此清晰地表达出来。

Shakespeare almost never used another verse form. He didn’t need to. It was the iambic pentameter or it was plain prose. Because the pentameter has an odd number of feet, it doesn’t need to rhyme. So Shakespeare could write conversations in it that sounded natural and normal. Yet still it always had that subtle beat tapping away underneath. It had a rhythm. Shakespeare could even cut up a pentameter and give each actor half. So Antony says to Cleopatra: ‘Com mand me!’

莎士比亚几乎从不使用其他诗体。他不需要。要么用抑扬格五音步，要么就用散文。因为五音步的音步数为奇数，所以不需要押韵。因此，莎士比亚可以用它写出自然流畅的对话。然而，对话中始终蕴含着一种微妙的节奏感。它有一种韵律。莎士比亚甚至可以把五音步拆分，让每个演员各说一半。比如，安东尼对克莉奥佩特拉说：“命令我！”

And Cleopatra replies: ‘ O , my par don!’

克利奥帕特拉回答说：“哦，我的错！”

And Antony replies: ‘ Now I must ’.

安东尼回答说：“现在我必须这么做了。”

And you stack ’em all together and get ‘Com mand me! O , my par don! Now I must ’. So the conversation can keep going without Shakespeare ever breaking the rhythm. The rhythm would get broken after a while, though. In general, Shakespeare has his heroes and his aristocrats natter away in iambic pentameters, but whenever the working classes come on stage they are forced to love, laugh and die in prose, because they’re common.

你把它们全部叠在一起，就得到了“命令我！哦，恕我冒昧！现在我必须这么做了”。这样，对话就能持续下去，莎士比亚的节奏也不会被打断。不过，节奏过一段时间后还是会被打破的。一般来说，莎士比亚笔下的英雄和贵族们都用抑扬格五音步闲聊，但每当劳动阶级出现在舞台上，他们就被迫用散文去爱、去笑、去死，因为他们是平民。

Shakespeare did write one play entirely in prose, but if you’ve ever seen or read The Life and Death of King John , you have my condolences. 1 Like all truly beautiful things, and people, the iambic pentameter gets boring after a while. That’s why the prose peasants are such a welcome relief. But on the smaller scale you break it up with variations. Just like the drum fill in the middle of a song, you can have a deliberate metrical break, just for the fun of it. Indeed, there are standard ways to do it. First, you can always add an extra syllable on the end:

莎士比亚确实写过一部完全用散文写成的戏剧，但如果你看过或读过《约翰王的生与死》，我深表同情。¹ 就像所有真正美好的事物和人一样，抑扬格五音步读久了也会让人感到乏味。这就是为什么散文如此令人耳目一新。但在较小的范围内，你可以用一些变化来打破这种单调。就像歌曲中间的鼓点填充一样，你可以故意打破一些韵律，纯粹是为了好玩。事实上，有一些标准的方法可以做到这一点。首先，你总是可以在结尾添加一个额外的音节：

To be , or not to be : that is the ques tion:

生存还是毁灭，这是一个问题：

The soft syllable simply slides into the pause at the end of the line. The other standard trick is to replace one of the iambs with a trochee, usually the first:

轻柔的音节直接滑入行尾的停顿处。另一个常用的技巧是用扬抑格替换其中一个抑扬格，通常是第一个：

Eye less in Ga za at the mill with slaves .

加沙的无眼奴隶在磨坊里。

Or you can do both:

或者你可以两者都做：

Whe ther ’tis nob ler in the mind to suff er

苦难是否在精神层面上更高尚

But you can put the trochee anywhere really, especially if you’re trying to sound all cracked and emotional. You just have to remember to get back in the rhythm afterwards.

但其实扬抑格可以放在任何位置，尤其是在你想表现得嘶哑而充满感情的时候。你只需要记住之后要重新找回节奏。

For God’s ¦ sake , let ¦ us sit up on the ground

看在上帝的份上，让我们坐在地上吧

And tell sad stor ies of the death of kings .

讲述国王之死的悲惨故事。

When he was in his twenties, Shakespeare was very careful about his pentameters. A little trochee here and there; an extra syllable there. By the time he was in his forties, he’d relaxed and would shuffle things around all the time. He even occasionally added an extra iamb onto the end of the line. That’s the sort of wildman, Devil-may-care versifier he was. But generally, his was a lifelong love affair with the iambic pentameter and almost all his most famous lines, from Romeo to Prospero, from nights Twelfth to Midsummer, go te-TUM te-TUM te-TUM te-TUM te-TUM.

莎士比亚二十多岁时，对五音步格律非常讲究。这里加个扬抑格，那里多加个音节。到了四十多岁，他就放松下来，经常随意调整格律。他甚至偶尔会在诗行末尾加一个抑扬格。他就是这样一位桀骜不驯、无所畏惧的诗人。但总的来说，他终其一生都钟爱抑扬格五音步，他几乎所有最著名的诗句，从《罗密欧与朱丽叶》到《普洛斯彼罗》，从《第十二夜》到《仲夏夜之梦》，都以抑扬格五音步写成。

Shakespeare didn’t invent the iambic pentameter. It had been the English standard ever since Geoffrey Chaucer began his crafty rhyming in the fourteenth century. Shakespeare simply leapt on a bandwagon and took charge. The iambic pentameter is the most natural form of English. It’s how the English language wants to be. And, in all seriousness, I didn’t even notice that that last sentence was one until I had typed it. 2

莎士比亚并非抑扬格五音步的发明者。自十四世纪杰弗里·乔叟开始运用其精妙的韵律以来，抑扬格五音步一直是英语的标准韵律。莎士比亚只不过是顺应潮流，将其发扬光大。抑扬格五音步是英语最自然的形式，它正是英语语言的本色。说真的，直到我打出最后那句话，我才意识到它也是抑扬格五音步。

The iambic pentameter remained the gold standard of English poetry. It’s reckoned that about three quarters of all English poetry is written in the meter. Milton used it for Paradise Lost . Pope used it for The Rape of the Lock . Wordsworth used it for The Prelude . Byron used it for Don Juan . And … well … everybody used it. Half the great lines you know are iambic pentameters.

抑扬格五音步一直是英国诗歌的黄金标准。据估计，大约四分之三的英国诗歌都是用这种格律写成的。弥尔顿在《失乐园》中用了它。蒲柏在《夺发记》中用了它。华兹华斯在《序曲》中用了它。拜伦在《唐璜》中用了它。而且……嗯……几乎所有人都用过它。你所知道的伟大诗句中，有一半都是抑扬格五音步。

Pro cras tin at ion is the thief of time (Edward Young, 1742)

拖延是时间的窃贼（爱德华·杨，1742 年）

They al so serve who on ly stand and wait . (John Milton, 1655)

那些只是站着等待的人，也同样是在服务。（约翰·弥尔顿，1655年）

To err is hum an, to for give div ine . (Alexander Pope, 1711)

人非圣贤，孰能无过；宽恕他人，乃是神圣之举。（亚历山大·蒲柏，1711年）

That last being an example of zeugma.

最后一个例子就是轭式修辞法。

1 To be fair, King John has one of the best speeches in Shakespeare. It’s just not worth reading the rest of the play to get there. Act III, scene iii. You’re welcome.

平心而论，《约翰王》中有一段莎士比亚戏剧中最精彩的独白。只是没必要为了这段独白而读完整部剧。第三幕第三场。不用谢。

2 At time of writing, there is a computer program called Pentametron that trawls Twitter looking for anyone who has accidentally written a perfect iambic pentameter. It then looks for another one that rhymes, and thus creates an unending, metrically perfect poem in rhyming couplets.

2 截至撰写本文时，有一个名为 Pentametron 的计算机程序，它会在 Twitter 上搜索任何无意中写出完美抑扬格五音步的人。然后它会寻找另一个与之押韵的五音步，从而创造出一首由押韵对句组成的、永无止境的、韵律完美的诗歌。

# ↩

Chapter 22

第22章

Zeugma

轭式

Zeugma (pronounced ZOOGmuh) is a funny little rhetorical figure that doesn’t work awfully well in English. Still, we might as well cover it. Other figures have produced loads of great lines; it some.

轭式修辞（发音为ZOOGmuh）是一种有趣的小修辞手法，在英语中不太适用。不过，我们不妨也介绍一下。其他修辞手法也创造了许多精彩的句子；其中一些也算。

Sometimes you have a series of clauses that all have the same verb. Tom likes whisky, Dick likes vodka, Harry likes crack cocaine . That’s three likes , but you only need one. Tom likes whisky, Dick vodka, Harry crack cocaine . The sentence still makes sense, because we understand that that first likes is still kind of hanging around in the next few clauses.

有时你会遇到一系列从句，它们都包含同一个动词。比如，汤姆喜欢威士忌，迪克喜欢伏特加，哈里喜欢快克可卡因。这里用了三个“喜欢”，但其实只需要一个动词就够了。句子应该是：汤姆喜欢威士忌，迪克喜欢伏特加，哈里喜欢快克可卡因。句子仍然通顺，因为我们明白第一个“喜欢”仍然贯穿于接下来的几个从句中。

With that in mind, let us turn to the most sexist and beautiful lines ever written in English: John Milton in Paradise Lost describing the essential differences between chaps and chapesses.

考虑到这一点，让我们来看看英语世界里最性别歧视、最优美的诗句：约翰·弥尔顿在《失乐园》中描述了绅士和淑女之间的本质区别。

For contemplation he and valour formed ,

他沉思冥想，同时又兼具勇气。

For softness she and sweet attractive grace;

她温柔甜美，风姿绰约；

He for God only, she for God in him.

他只为上帝，她为他里面的上帝而活。

Formed , like one of those upmarket lavatory cleaners, keeps working, even after the flush. Strangely, though, Milton’s sentence works. It feels natural in a way that a lot of zeugmas don’t. Shakespeare uses the device lots and it always has something of a weird flavour. So Juliet and Romeo run into a little family dispute, ‘But passion lends them power, time means, to meet’. Of course, time is lending them means, but it takes a little moment to work that out. And ‘How Tarquin wronged me, I Collatine’ sounds just plain wrong in English. If Shakespeare has trouble with a trick, you know it’s hard.

就像那些高档的厕所清洁剂一样，即使冲水后，它仍然有效。奇怪的是，弥尔顿的这句话却很流畅自然，很多轭式修辞手法都做不到这一点。莎士比亚经常使用这种修辞手法，但它总是带有一种怪异的韵味。比如，朱丽叶和罗密欧遇到了一点家庭纠纷，“但激情赋予他们力量，时间让他们相遇”。当然，时间赋予了他们相遇的可能，但这需要一点时间才能理解。“塔奎因如何冤枉了我，我，科拉廷”这句话用英语听起来就很别扭。如果连莎士比亚都觉得某个技巧很难，那你就知道它有多难了。

Zeugma does have its moments. It makes things sound crisp and clear. You start with a full and florid sentence and then you’re down to a bunch of nouns. The first clause sounds normal, the second curt. Zeugma’s for the kind of taciturn guy who doesn’t waste time on main verbs, or breath on you.

轭式修辞法确实有其妙处。它能让句子听起来简洁明了。开头用华丽的辞藻堆砌句子，然后突然变成一堆名词。第一个分句听起来很自然，第二个分句则显得简短有力。轭式修辞法适合那种沉默寡言、不愿在主要动词上浪费时间、甚至懒得跟你说话的人。

So it works very well occasionally, but only if you want to sound dismissive, as Oscar Wilde did when he said: ‘The good end happily and the bad unhappily. That is what fiction means.’ It’s also what Tennyson used when he had Ulysses dismiss his son’s entire life with the words ‘He works his work; I mine.’

所以，这种说法偶尔确实很管用，但前提是你想要表达一种轻蔑的态度，就像奥斯卡·王尔德那样，他说：“好人有好结局，坏人有坏结局。这就是小说的意义。” 丁尼生也用过这种手法，他让尤利西斯用“他做他的工作，我做我的工作”这句话来否定儿子的一生。

If a very strict grammarian were listening to Ulysses, he might point out that ‘He works his work; I works mine’ is grammatically all wrong. But it takes a very odd kind of mind to notice that sort of thing. 1 When Othello is told that his wife ‘has deceived a father, and may thee’, the meaning is obvious and nobody would pick up the error without a notepad and too much spare time.

如果一位非常严谨的语法学家在听《尤利西斯》，他可能会指出“他做他的工作；我做我的工作”在语法上完全错误。但只有思维非常独特的人才能注意到这种细节。当奥赛罗被告知他的妻子“欺骗了一位父亲，也可能欺骗你”时，意思显而易见，除非拿着笔记本并花费大量时间，否则没人会注意到其中的错误。

Usually, zeugma has the verb actually printed in the first clause and then understood in the second (prozeugma). But you can do it the other way around and have the verb in the last clause (hypozeugma). It’s even weirder in English, because English is a nice, sequential language where things happen in a sensible order, unlike Latin. But it can be carried off. Shakespeare managed it well once. ‘As you on him, Demetrius dote on you.’ But that’s hardly his greatest line.

通常，轭式修辞中动词会直接出现在第一个分句中，然后在第二个分句中隐含（前轭式修辞）。但你也可以反过来，把动词放在最后一个分句中（后轭式修辞）。这在英语中显得更加奇怪，因为英语是一种优美、循序渐进的语言，事物的发生顺序合乎逻辑，这与拉丁语截然不同。但这种修辞手法并非不可行。莎士比亚就曾巧妙地运用过一次：“你爱他，狄米特律斯也爱你。”但这并非他最伟大的台词。

There are two reasons that zeugma doesn’t really work in English. First, we’re not used to seeing verbs miles away from their nouns. The Romans were, and they loved it in a way that makes schoolchildren despair. We can just about manage it here and there, but it’s a shock. The second reason is that we would much rather balance clauses in an isocolon (q.v.). ‘My true love hath my heart and I have his’ wouldn’t be nearly as beautiful if it were ‘My true love hath my heart, I his’, or even ‘My true love my heart, I have his’, which is, frankly, gibberish.

英语中“轭式修辞”不太适用有两个原因。首先，我们不习惯看到动词和名词相距甚远。罗马人却很擅长这种修辞手法，而且他们对此的喜爱程度，简直让小学生都感到绝望。我们偶尔也能勉强使用，但感觉很突兀。第二个原因是，我们更倾向于用等长句（参见相关条目）来平衡句子结构。“My true love hasth my heart and I have his”如果改成“My true love hasth my heart, I his”，或者甚至是“My true love my heart, I have his”，就远没有那么优美了，后者简直莫名其妙。

Poor zeugma! So elegant in the classical world! So silly in ours! Like a toga.

可怜的轭式修辞！在古典世界里如此优雅！在我们这个时代却如此愚蠢！就像一件托加长袍。

There are a few really famous phrases that use zeugma. It’s just that you don’t know them. The best measure of a rhetorical figure is how it survives or dies in the popular memory. So some tricks, like diacope, are remembered even when they didn’t happen (see Chapter 12 ); zeugma isn’t even when it did.

有一些非常著名的短语运用了轭式修辞手法，只是你不知道而已。衡量一种修辞手法好坏的最佳标准是它在大众记忆中的存续情况。因此，有些修辞技巧，比如双关，即使从未出现过，人们也会记住（参见第十二章）；而轭式修辞手法即便出现过，也鲜为人知。

In 1697 a tragedy by William Congreve was all, or at least most of the rage in London. It was called The Mourning Bride and opened with the line ‘Music hath charms to soothe the savage breast’. It doesn’t quite keep up that standard, but it’s really Not Too Bad.

1697年，威廉·康格里夫的悲剧《哀悼的新娘》风靡伦敦，至少在当时是如此。这部剧以“音乐有抚慰野蛮心灵的魔力”开篇。虽然它未能完全达到这个水准，但其实也还不错。

There’s a character in The Mourning Bride called Zara who’s a bit of a bunny-boiler. She’s in love with Osmyn, and doesn’t realise that not only is Osmyn secretly married to a princess, but that he’s not called Osmyn at all. Anyway, she discovers that he and the princess are all sighs and cuddles and decides to work their downfall, or more precisely to have Osmyn (not his real name) executed. She tells him in his prison cell:

《哀悼的新娘》里有个叫扎拉的角色，她有点儿神经质。她爱上了奥斯敏，却不知道奥斯敏不仅秘密娶了一位公主，而且他的真名根本不叫奥斯敏。总之，她发现奥斯敏和公主腻歪在一起，于是决定扳倒他们，更准确地说，是想把奥斯敏（化名）处死。她在奥斯敏的牢房里对他说：

Vile and ingrate! too late thou shalt repent

卑鄙无耻，忘恩负义！你悔改为时已晚。

The base injustice thou hast done my love:

你对我的爱人犯下了何等卑劣的罪行：

Yes, thou shalt know, spite of thy past distress,

是的，尽管你过去经历过苦难，你终将明白。

And all those ills which thou so long hast mourned;

以及你长久以来所哀悼的所有苦难；

Heav’n has no rage, like love to hatred turned,

天堂没有愤怒，就像爱转为恨一样。

Nor hell a fury, like a woman scorned.

也比不上被轻视的女人那样愤怒。

The line is immortal, but not as a zeugma. We chuck a hath straight back in (‘hell hath no fury, like a woman scorned’), because the popular memory cannot abide the elision. Congreve was probably rather proud of writing the line, but then, as it saith in the Bible, ‘pride goeth before destruction and a haughty spirit before a fall’; universally remembered as ‘pride goes before a fall’.

这句诗名垂青史，但并非以轭式修辞手法流传下来。我们直接把“hath”加了回去（“地狱的怒火也比不上被轻蔑的女人”），因为人们的记忆无法容忍省略。康格里夫或许对写出这句诗颇为自豪，但正如《圣经》所说，“骄傲在败坏以先，狂妄在跌倒之前”；而人们普遍记住的却是“骄傲在跌倒之前”。

Zeugma is a weak figure: good for expressing contempt, and contemptible in other expressions. Can it be improved? ‘Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?’ (Jeremiah 13, verse 23)

轭式修辞是一种较弱的修辞手法：它适合表达轻蔑，但在其他表达方式中则显得卑劣。它能否改进呢？“古实人岂能改变肤色呢？豹岂能改变斑点呢？”（耶利米书 13:23）

So the memorable phrases that employed zeugma prove that zeugma isn’t memorable. This is a paradox.

因此，那些运用轭式修辞手法而令人印象深刻的短语，反而证明了轭式修辞手法本身并不令人难忘。这真是一个悖论。

1 Very, very, very technically, some scholars (but not all) say that it’s zeugma only when it’s grammatically wrong. But that applies more to Latin than English.

1. 从非常非常非常严谨的角度来说，一些学者（但并非所有学者）认为，只有语法错误才算是轭式修辞。但这更多地适用于拉丁语而非英语。

# ↩

Chapter 23

第23章

Paradox

悖论

Paradoxes are remarkably hard to define, but you know one when you see one. Mathematicians, logicians, psychologists, sociologists and poets all compete for the word. They all think they own it. But this is untrue. For paradoxes are quite paradoxical.

悖论很难定义，但你一眼就能认出来。数学家、逻辑学家、心理学家、社会学家和诗人都在争夺这个词的使用权，他们都认为自己拥有它。但事实并非如此。因为悖论本身就充满了悖论。

Let’s start with Oscar Wilde, master of inversion. Most of Wilde’s paradoxes are not paradoxes at all. They are simply simple thoughts expressed in a terribly surprising way.

让我们先从奥斯卡·王尔德说起，他是反转大师。王尔德的大多数悖论根本就不是悖论，它们只是以一种极其出人意料的方式表达的简单思想。

In this world there are only two tragedies. One is not getting what one wants, and the other is getting it.

世上只有两种悲剧：一种是得不到自己想要的东西，另一种是得到了自己想要的东西。

– Oscar Wilde, Lady Windermere’s Fan , 1892

——奥斯卡·王尔德，《温德米尔夫人的扇子》，1892年

There are two tragedies in life. One is to lose your heart’s desire. The other is to gain it.

人生有两大悲剧：一是失去心仪之物，二是得到它。

– George Bernard Shaw, Man and Superman , 1903

——乔治·萧伯纳，《人与超人》，1903年

Really, there’s no paradox here. You or I might have said ‘screwed either way’, but not Wilde. He simply sets the sentence up as though it’s going to mention two separate things, and then doubles back on himself. The content is not paradoxical. The phrasing is. And as a result the audience are just as pleased as they would have been if Wilde had invented a real paradox. It is style not substance that counts, and the superficial qualities that last, even when the deeper nature has been found out.

其实，这里并没有什么悖论。你我或许会说“反正都完了”，但王尔德不会。他只是把句子写得好像要提到两件不同的事情，然后又自相矛盾地回到了原点。内容本身并不悖论，悖论在于措辞。因此，观众的感受和王尔德真的创造了一个悖论时一样，都同样感到愉悦。风格而非内容才是最重要的，表面的特质经久不衰，即便其更深层的本质已被揭示。

Exactly the same thing goes with:

同样的情况也适用于：

There is only one thing in the world worse than being talked about, and that is not being talked about.

世界上只有一件事比被人议论更糟糕，那就是无人议论。

It’s not a paradox, but a statement of grumpy resignation. But it is phrased like a paradox. To borrow a term from logic, it is a veridical paradox, one that only appears impossible, but is in fact quite simple. Wilde pushes this trick a little further with:

这并非悖论，而是一种愤懑无奈的陈述。但它的措辞却像悖论。借用逻辑学中的一个术语，这是一个“真实悖论”，它看似不可能，实则非常简单。王尔德更进一步，提出了这个技巧：

All women become like their mothers. That is their tragedy. No man does, and that is his.

所有女人最终都会变得像她们的母亲。这是她们的悲剧。男人则不会，这是男人的悲剧。

This could have been phrased, ‘Why is it that your girlfriend’s mother is always annoying, but your male friends’ mothers are always lovely?’ But instead, it was phrased as a veridical paradox. Wilde does do real paradoxes, but I’ll come to them when I’ve dealt with puns.

这句话原本可以这样问：“为什么你女朋友的妈妈总是那么烦人，而你男性朋友的妈妈却总是那么可爱？” 但作者却把它写成了一个真正的悖论。王尔德确实会使用真正的悖论，不过等我讲完双关语之后再谈吧。

The pun-paradox is, perhaps, the runt of the litter. It is at the same time a paradox and merely a pun. Both and neither. When Crystal Gayle sang ‘Don’t It Make My Brown Eyes Blue’ she was, at the same time, contradicting Wittgenstein’s axiom that no part of the visual field can simultaneously be of two hues, and making a statement that anybody familiar with the English language will find unexceptionable, as unexceptionable as John Lennon’s assertion that red was the colour that would make him blue or his complaint that he was both black and blue. British politics was altered by such a paradox with the most famous poster in electoral history: a queue of people snaking away into the distance, and the slogan ‘Labour Isn’t Working’. The people in the queue were all actually very well-employed, at Conservative Central Office, but the paradox was perfect. Politics is full of potential for such things, but for some reason nobody has used the slogan ‘The Left is Right’, or ‘The Right is Wrong’ (aside from the Johnny Cash song ‘The One on the Right Is on the Left’). The punning paradox is, perhaps, no paradox at all, but it is intriguing and it is memorable, and Back to the Future made a tidy profit.

双关悖论或许是所有双关语中最不起眼的一个。它既是悖论，又是双关语。两者兼具，又非此即彼。当克丽丝塔尔·盖尔演唱《难道我的棕色眼睛不蓝吗？》时，她一方面反驳了维特根斯坦关于视觉领域中任何部分不可能同时呈现两种色调的公理，另一方面又表达了一个任何熟悉英语的人都会觉得无可挑剔的观点，就像约翰·列侬声称红色会让他感到忧郁，或者抱怨自己既是黑色又是蓝色一样。英国政治也因这样一个悖论而改变，其中最著名的选举海报便是：一条蜿蜒延伸至远方的队伍，以及“工党不干活”的标语。队伍中的人实际上都在保守党中央办公室工作，收入颇丰，但这个悖论却完美地诠释了这一点。政治领域充满了这种可能性，但不知为何，除了约翰尼·卡什的歌曲《右边的人其实是左边的人》之外，没人用过“左派是对的”或“右派是错的”这样的口号。这种双关悖论或许根本算不上悖论，但它引人入胜，令人难忘，《回到未来》也因此赚得盆满钵满。

But the pun leads us closer to the true paradox, because it at least looks like one. When Oscar Wilde said that ‘We live in an age when unnecessary things are our only necessities’ he was still being veridical, but he was heading towards the central contradiction. Luxury is, for the human, a necessity; what are commonly called the necessities can usually be dispensed with. Chance is a certainty and living is only the slow process of dying. And here we find ourselves pushing towards the ‘what it’s all about’, but only pushing so far. Even Shakespeare saying ‘I must be cruel only to be kind’ didn’t push his foot over the threshold. Wilde never clasped the full and fascinating contradiction, he never said anything that didn’t make sense, or make you laugh, after a few moments’ thought. He would do anything for a good paradox, but he wouldn’t do that.
