Peroration

结语

Shakespeare even told us how to use the figures: ‘And practise rhetoric in your common talk.’ We do, anyway, to some extent. There is no figure that I’ve written up here, that you have not, at some time, used. This book is only a looking glass, in which you can see the best of your words.

莎士比亚甚至告诉我们如何运用修辞格：“在日常谈话中练习修辞。” 无论如何，我们多少都会这样做。我在这里列举的每一个修辞格，你们都曾在某个时候使用过。这本书就像一面镜子，让你们从中看到自己言辞中最精彩的部分。

The aim of this book has been to make clear what is done, a clarity and knowledge that has been abandoned for a couple of centuries now. It is as though we had decided to forget about structural engineering, and instead build our buildings by chance. Any figure overused, or used in the wrong place and at the wrong time, will be a fault. But a figure used and used well, is the beauty of the English language.

本书旨在阐明建筑的运作方式，这种清晰的认识和知识已被我们遗忘了几个世纪。仿佛我们放弃了结构工程，转而凭运气建造房屋。任何数字，如果使用不当，或用在不恰当的地方，都会成为缺陷。但恰当且恰当地运用数字，正是英语语言之美。

Above all, I hope I have dispelled the bleak and imbecilic idea that the aim of writing is to express yourself clearly in plain, simple English using as few words as possible. This is a fiction, a fib, a fallacy, a fantasy and a falsehood. To write for mere utility is as foolish as to dress for mere utility. Mountaineers do it, and climb Everest in clothes that would have you laughed out of the gutter. I suspect they also communicate quickly and efficiently, poor things. But for the rest of us, not threatened by death and yetis, clothes and language can be things of beauty. I would no more write without art because I didn’t need to, than I would wander outdoors naked just because it was warm enough. Again.

首先，我希望我已经驳斥了那种悲观而愚蠢的想法：写作的目的就是用尽可能少的词语，以简洁明了的英语清晰地表达自己。这纯属虚构，是谎言，是谬论，是幻想，是谎言。仅仅为了实用而写作，就像仅仅为了实用而穿衣一样愚蠢。登山者确实如此，他们穿着那些会让你笑掉大牙的衣服攀登珠穆朗玛峰。我猜想，他们也能快速有效地沟通，真是可怜。但对于我们这些不受死亡和雪人威胁的人来说，衣服和语言也可以是美的化身。我不会因为不需要就放弃艺术而写作，就像我不会因为天气暖和就裸奔一样。再说一遍。

These figures grow like wildflowers, but they can be cultivated too. I do not believe that The Beatles had any idea what anadiplosis was, any more than I believe that the Rolling Stones knew about syllepsis. They knew what worked, and it did.

这些人物形象如同野花般自然生长，但也可以人为塑造。我不认为披头士乐队了解什么是叠句，就像我不认为滚石乐队了解叠句一样。他们只知道什么有效，而且确实有效。

The figures of rhetoric are the beauties of all the poems we have ever read. Without them we would merely be us: eating, sleeping, manufacturing and dying. With them everything can be glorious. For though we have nothing to say, we can at least say it well.

修辞手法是所有我们读过的诗歌之美。没有它们，我们不过是平凡的我们：吃饭、睡觉、生产、死亡。有了它们，一切都可以熠熠生辉。因为即便我们无话可说，至少也能说得精彩绝伦。

Epilogue Concerning Terminology

关于术语的结语

Rhetorical terminology is a catastrophe and a mess.

修辞术语简直是一场灾难，一团糟。

Rhetoric was invented by the Ancient Greeks, who thought up lots of lovely Ancient Greek words for the patterns they’d found. But different writers defined these words a little differently. Some used them loosely, some very precisely and some used them with a different meaning altogether.

修辞学是由古希腊人发明的，他们创造了许多优美的古希腊词汇来描述他们发现的各种修辞模式。但不同的作家对这些词汇的定义略有不同。有些人使用得比较宽泛，有些人则非常精确，还有一些人赋予了它们完全不同的含义。

Then came the Romans. Sometimes they used the Greek terms, and sometimes they thought up their own. And then they got all muddled and used the words in different ways or didn’t define them properly at all.

后来罗马人来了。他们有时用希腊语词汇，有时又自创词汇。结果他们把事情搞得一团糟，要么用词各异，要么干脆就没给词下正确的定义。

Then came the medieval monks, each sitting in a different monastery, each reading and adapting different Greek and Roman books on rhetoric and muddling things still further.

然后是中世纪的僧侣们，他们各自坐在不同的修道院里，阅读和改编不同的希腊罗马修辞学书籍，进一步把事情搞得一团糟。

Then came the Renaissance. Everybody started rediscovering Ancient Rhetoric and adapting it to their own language, even if it didn’t fit properly. Puttenham and Peacham and other people beginning with P produced dictionaries of rhetoric in English, which weren’t quite the same as the Ancients’, but were sort of good enough.

随后文艺复兴到来。人们开始重新发现古代修辞学，并将其融入自己的语言，即便并不完全契合。普特纳姆、皮查姆以及其他一些名字以字母P开头的人编纂了英语修辞学词典，虽然与古代的词典略有不同，但也算得上足够用了。

To solve this almighty muddle Puttenham decided to invent a whole new batch of English terms with lovely names like ‘the cuckoo-spell’ and ‘the slow return’. They didn’t catch on, and modern books on rhetoric sneer and chortle at him, which is quite unfair.

为了解决这个巨大的混乱局面，普特纳姆决定发明一大堆新的英语术语，并赋予它们诸如“布谷鸟咒语”和“缓慢回归”这样优美的名字。这些术语并没有流行起来，现代修辞学书籍对他嗤之以鼻，这很不公平。

Usually, this sort of thing got straightened out in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries when the great reference works started to be written. But unfortunately that was the time when rhetoric was out of fashion, and thus the confusion only got confused further. The Oxford Dictionary of Literary Terms and the Oxford English Dictionary have completely different definitions of zeugma.

通常，这类问题会在十九世纪和二十世纪随着重要参考著作的编纂而得到解决。但不幸的是，当时修辞学并不流行，因此这种混乱反而加剧了。《牛津文学术语词典》和《牛津英语词典》对“轭式修辞”（zeugma）的定义截然不同。

The result of all this is that every technical rhetorical term has had fourteen different definitions, and that every figure of rhetoric has had fourteen different names. The standard modern dictionary of rhetoric – Lanham’s A Handlist of Rhetorical Terms – makes a point of listing all of the alternative names, and all the alternative meanings. If you want to be absolutely sure of the terminology, you should burn this book, and buy Lanham.

这一切的结果是，每个修辞学术语都有十四个不同的定义，每一种修辞手法都有十四个不同的名称。现代修辞学标准词典——兰汉的《修辞术语手册》——特意列出了所有别名和别义。如果你想绝对确定术语的正确性，你应该把这本书烧掉，然后去买兰汉的词典。

This is not a dictionary of rhetoric, nor was it meant to be.

这不是一本修辞学词典，也并非旨在成为一本修辞学词典。

There’s also the problem that the lines between this historical figure and that are often very blurry. Careful readers may have noticed that diacope (Crisis? What crisis?) is very similar to epanalepsis (beginning and ending a sentence with the same word), and that epanalepsis is closely related to chiasmus (symmetrical sentence structure) and so on and so forth. Epizeuxis (repeating the same word) is necessarily alliterative and pleonastic and …

还有一个问题是，这个历史人物和那个人物之间的界限往往非常模糊。细心的读者可能已经注意到，diacope（危机？什么危机？）与epanalepsis（句首句尾用同一个词）非常相似，而epanalepsis又与chiasmus（对称句式结构）密切相关，等等。Epizeuxis（重复同一个词）必然是头韵和赘述，而且……

You get the picture, and it ain’t a pretty one.

你应该明白我的意思了，情况不妙。

However, it’s a truth of all the humanities that you have to learn the distinctions first, and only then can you learn why the distinctions don’t really exist. Therefore, I’ve kept everything in its own little chapter away from its relatives, and given each thing one name.

然而，人文学科的普遍真理是，你必须先了解它们之间的区别，才能明白为什么这些区别实际上并不存在。因此，我把每件事都单独放在一个章节里，与它们之间的关联区分开来，并且给每件事都起了个名字。

The purpose of this book has been to show how rhetoric is used in English. Each chapter has tried to identify a figure and illustrate what effect it has using famous examples from the last 500 years. Each one has been given a name that just about fits, but a rose that is called henprosoparapanadiploeia is a rose is a rose is a rose.

本书旨在展示英语中修辞手法的运用。每一章都试图识别一种修辞格，并用过去500年间的著名例子来说明其效果。每个修辞格都被赋予了一个大致贴切的名称，但一朵名为henprosoparapanadiploeia的玫瑰，它就是一朵玫瑰，它就是一朵玫瑰。

However, there are stern and serious scholars who try to sort out this jungle. There are those who would snort at my definition of subjectio, fly into a rage over my views of syllepsis, and, upon reading my definition of scesis onomaton would actually write a letter. Indeed, it occurs to me, dear reader, that you may actually be one of those stern and serious scholars. It’s possible. If you are, I would be delighted never to hear from you. Seriously. Take that letter, roll it up, wrap it in brambles, and stick it somewhere that alliter… [continued in Chapter 1 ].

然而，总有一些严谨认真的学者试图厘清这片迷雾。有些人会对我关于subjectio的定义嗤之以鼻，对我关于syllepsis的观点勃然大怒，甚至在读到我对scesis onomaton的定义后，还会写信来找我。亲爱的读者，我突然想到，您或许就是这些严谨认真的学者之一。这并非不可能。如果您真是如此，我倒希望永远不要收到您的来信。真的。把那封信卷起来，用荆棘包裹起来，然后把它塞到某个……（未完待续，见第一章）

Selected Further Reading

延伸阅读推荐

A Handlist of Rhetorical Terms – Richard A. Lanham (the standard reference work)

修辞术语手册——理查德·A·兰汉姆（标准参考著作）

Shakespeare’s Use of the Arts of Language – Sister Miriam Joseph (not with a bang but a wimple)

莎士比亚对语言艺术的运用——米里亚姆·约瑟夫修女（不是以爆炸声，而是以头巾）

Classical Rhetoric in English Poetry – Professor Sir Brian Vickers (an excellent introduction)

英语诗歌中的古典修辞学——布莱恩·维克斯爵士教授（一本极佳的入门读物）

In Defence of Rhetoric – Professor Sir Brian Vickers (a comprehensive vindication)

为修辞学辩护——布莱恩·维克斯爵士教授（全面辩护）

You Talkin’ To Me? – Sam Leith (an introduction to the more structural aspects of rhetoric and persuasion, as opposed to the verbal figures found here)

你在跟我说话吗？——萨姆·莱斯（本书介绍修辞和说服的结构性方面，而非此处涉及的修辞格）

And on the internet

在互联网上

Silva Rhetoricae ( rhetoric.byu.edu ), produced by Gideon O. Burton of Brigham Young University (a dictionary listing alternative names and definitions in which one can click happily between related terms)

Silva Rhetoricae (rhetoric.byu.edu)，由杨百翰大学的 Gideon O. Burton 制作（一个列出不同名称和定义的词典，用户可以在相关术语之间轻松点击）。
